title: Team SouL’s PMGC 2026 Participation at Risk as Half the Squad Still Waits for Turkey Visas
content:
Half of Team SouL’s players are still waiting for Turkish visas days before the PUBG Mobile Global Championship (PMGC) 2026, putting India’s only team at the event at risk of missing it. S8UL’s Sid said on 19 November that some players have received their visas while the rest still show as under process.

Sid warned that the team’s participation “will be at a risk” if the remaining visas do not arrive by 20 November. He tagged the Turkish Consulate General in Mumbai and asked it to help the team travel in time to represent India.

Sid posted the appeal on X, describing it as an urgent request for support. He wrote that iQOO SouL had officially qualified for PMGC 2026, which is being held in Turkey, and that only half of the squad had been cleared so far.

Urgent request for support regarding our pending Turkey visas. Our team, IQOO SOUL, officially qualified for the PUBG MOBILE Global Championship (PMGC) which will be held in Turkey. Half of our team has received their visas while the other half still shows under process. If we…

He asked the Turkish Embassy in Mumbai to look into the matter and asked fans to share the post for more visibility. The post passed 104,000 views within hours, along with more than 2,300 reposts, 3,300 likes and over 900 replies. Many replies came from Indian esports fans and creators tagging officials and urging a quick decision on the pending applications.

The Turkish consulate in Mumbai had not responded publicly at the time of writing. Sid did not say which players are still waiting or give a reason for the delay. If the remaining visas are not issued in time, SouL would have to decide whether to travel with part of the squad, field substitutes or withdraw, though the team has not discussed any of those options publicly.

Dota 2 Receives Major 7.42 Patch: Massive Changes, New Hero Tease, and More
content:
While gamers around the world were busy tuning in to GTA 6, Valve rolled out a major Dota 2 update that reshapes the game at its core. The highly anticipated Dota 2 Patch 7.42 went live at around 8 am UTC on November 19, and it changes the economy, the map, items, and most of the game’s hero roster, while also teasing what many players believe to be a brand-new hero.

Here’s everything you need to know about Dota 2’s latest update before you hop on your next ranked game.

The biggest highlight of the Dota 2 patch 7.42 is the fundamental change to hero stats. Base health for every hero in the game has been raised from 120 to 200, with each point of Strength now giving 20 health instead of 22.

The magic resistance from the Intelligence stat has also been raised from 0.1% to 0.125%. Additionally, the patch also tones down spell damage across the board and cuts some long-lasting slows, so fights should be a little less explosive.

Valve has added an “Item Potency” mechanic to Dota 2 with the 7.42 patch. Attacks from heroes (and hero-like units, including illusions) will now have an attribute called Item Potency . Effects from items like Desolator and Eye of Skadi now scale with the attack’s Item Potency, with illusions only getting a fraction of the full effect.

There’s also a crucial change to the game’s economy, as passive gold income no longer grows as the game goes on, and rewards for destroying buildings have been standardized and reduced across the board.

title: Rockstar Tells Tribunal Sacked Staff ‘Flouted’ Rules as Union Vote Runs Through GTA 6 Launch
content:
Rockstar Games spent the final days before Grand Theft Auto VI’s release defending itself at an employment tribunal in Glasgow, while more than 1,600 of its UK staff are eligible to vote on recognising a union. The case was brought by 23 former employees who say they were sacked for trade union activity, a claim Rockstar denies. Closing submissions were heard on 17 and 18 November, and no date has been set for a judgment.

The two events now overlap with the biggest launch in the studio’s history. The union recognition ballot opened on 12 November and closes on 26 November, so voting runs through launch week. The game itself went live around the world on 19 November, with our GTA 6 launch live blog tracking each regional unlock.

About 34 people were dismissed across the UK and Canada in October 2025, according to the Press Association . Rockstar says they were let go for gross misconduct after confidential company information was shared on a Discord server with hundreds of members. Its barrister, Thomas Cordrey, told the tribunal that the dismissals came down to the “flouting of contractual policies and obligations”.

“We know the policies, we know our employer would be opposed to the use of a semi-public Discord,” Cordrey also said in his closing. Rockstar’s case is that the workers knew the rules and broke them, rather than being targeted for joining a union. The case is being heard at the Glasgow Tribunals Centre before Employment Judge Lucy Wiseman, and our report from the October hearings covered earlier evidence about the Discord server.

Rockstar has stood by its decision throughout the case. “Individuals across the UK and Canada were dismissed for gross misconduct,” a spokesperson said, adding that the company remains “confident of a positive outcome”. The studio has not linked the dispute to the game’s release, and its public launch message from co-founder Sam Houser focused on players.

The 23 claimants are represented by the Independent Workers’ Union of Great Britain, known as the IWGB. Their lawyer, Richard O’Keeffe, argued in his closing submission that managers had known about the Discord server for around three years, according to a separate Press Association report . He said Rockstar acted only in October 2025, when IWGB membership was nearing 10% of the workforce.

title: Inner Circle play on after owner Slobozhenko is detained in Italy
content:
The Ukrainian side face GamerLegion on Thursday with no word from the organisation about its owner, who is wanted in Ukraine over alleged tax evasion.

Inner Circle have not said a word about their owner. Oleksandr Slobozhenko, the 28-year-old Ukrainian influencer who founded the marketing company Traffic Devils and owns the CS2 organisation, has been detained in Italy at the request of Ukraine’s Economic Security Bureau (ESB), Ukrainska Pravda reported on Wednesday. The paper’s sources in law enforcement say he was detained at a hotel on Tuesday 17 November.

Italian police acted on a Ukrainian warrant after he checked into a hotel in Riccione, near Rimini, according to the Kyiv Independent . Ukraine’s Prosecutor General’s Office told Babel that prosecutors are preparing the documents to ask Italy to hand him over. No extradition has been agreed.

The ESB suspects Slobozhenko of evading about UAH 213 million (around €4.3 million) in taxes on income earned between January 2020 and August 2023, and of laundering the proceeds. The Kyiv Independent lists illegal gambling among the suspicions, which the ESB filed in 2023 and 2024. According to the bureau, his company was never registered as a legal entity in Ukraine, and the earnings were hidden through crypto wallets and illegal currency exchange.

“The suspect’s trusted individuals registered cryptocurrency wallets using their personal details and documents,” the ESB said, as quoted by the Kyiv Independent.

These are suspicions, not convictions. A court ordered his detention in absentia in 2024.

title: How to play Deadlock: getting access and your first matches

That sounds harder than it is. Anyone with the game can invite as many Steam friends as they like, and the invite is free. Here is how to get in, and what to do once you are.

The invite has to come from someone on your Steam friends list who already has Deadlock.

The invite thread on the fan-run Deadlock Community Discord, the Deadlock forums on Steam and the invite megathread on r/DeadlockTheGame are full of players who hand out invites. Add them as a Steam friend, and they send it.

It can take a few minutes or a few hours. If nothing shows up, check the playtest invites page in your Steam account.

title: N3on Becomes First Player to Finish GTA 6 Story Mode, Completes It in Just 7 Hours
content:
American streamer N3on has completed the full story mode of Grand Theft Auto VI in about seven hours, making him the first player known to finish the campaign since launch. He reached the ending live on stream, far faster than the playtime estimates that had circulated before release.

The run has divided viewers. Many players have questioned how the game’s full story could be finished so quickly, while others accused N3on of rushing through every mission instead of playing the game properly.

N3on started GTA 6 when it unlocked on 19 November and played straight through the main campaign on stream. He reached the end credits after roughly seven hours of play, skipping side activities and heading directly from one story mission to the next.

The campaign is split into five chapters with 93 main story missions, as listed in the full GTA 6 chapters and missions list . Finishing all of them in seven hours works out to well under five minutes per mission on average, which many fans have called hard to believe.

Rockstar Games has not commented on the run or confirmed how many players have reached the ending so far. Full footage from the stream had not been independently checked at the time of writing.

Before launch, the most cited figure came from Rockstar North co studio head Rob Nelson, who said his own playthrough took about 80 hours. That figure included optional goals with narrative consequences, not just the main story. Leaks before release suggested a main story of around 50 to 75 hours, which led many fans to expect a campaign of about 70 hours.

title: PSN Down Minutes After GTA 6 Launches in the US, PlayStation Store Goes Offline in Europe As Well
content:
Update, 6:02am UTC, 19 November: PlayStation’s status page no longer lists any problem in the Americas, so PS5 and PS4 players in the US, Canada and Latin America should be able to launch games again. The gaming and social problem in the UK and Europe has cleared too. Sony still lists a PlayStation Store outage for that region, now with a start time of 5:56am UTC.

PlayStation Network is having problems again, barely half an hour after Grand Theft Auto VI went live in the US and Canada. PlayStation’s official status page marked its “Gaming and social” service as degraded on PS5 and PS4 across the Americas at 5:33am UTC on 19 November. Sony’s notice warns that players “might have difficulty launching games, apps, or network features”, and says it is working to fix the issue as soon as possible.

The problem is not limited to North America. A minute later, at 5:34am UTC, the status page for the UK, Europe, the Middle East, Australia and New Zealand showed the same degraded gaming service and a full outage for the PlayStation Store. Sony’s store notice says players “might have difficulty getting products in PlayStation Store”, which hits anyone still trying to buy GTA VI on launch night.

GTA VI unlocked across the US and Canada at 5am UTC, which was midnight on the East Coast. The US unlock happened at the same moment in every time zone, so players in Chicago could start at 11pm, Denver at 10pm and Los Angeles at 9pm on 18 November. Rockstar’s support page on release times says the game releases at midnight local time in all regions.

US storefronts treated the whole country as a single release region keyed to Eastern time, as Forbes reported last week, and that is how the launch played out. Every US player could start at once, rather than in waves an hour apart, so West Coast players got the game three hours before their own midnight. Sony’s degraded notice for the Americas appeared 33 minutes after that unlock, and the notice does not give a cause.

Players who have already downloaded the game may still be able to start it, depending on how their PS5 is set up. Digital games usually run without a connection on a console that has Console Sharing and Offline Play turned on, which is normally switched on for the first PS5 an account signs into. You can check it under Settings, then Users and Accounts, then Other, then Console Sharing and Offline Play.

title: Best Axion loadout in Modern Warfare 4 multiplayer
content:
The Axion is one of the better assault rifles in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 , but it still needs the best possible loadout if you want to succeed with it in multiplayer. The Axion is a reliable choice for players that’s great at medium and long ranges, being more of a traditional AR. However, equipping the right attachments is still needed to get the most out of the Axion in Modern Warfare 4.

Below, you can find our recommended Axion loadout to use in Modern Warfare 4 multiplayer.

The Axion is a solid all-around assault rifle, so we really don’t have to focus on a single key area with its loadout. title: Take-Two Adds Billions in Market Value as GTA 6 Launches, Shares Close Up 6%
content:
Take-Two Interactive added billions of dollars to its stock market value on 18 November as Grand Theft Auto VI began rolling out worldwide. The publisher’s shares closed at $216.54, up 6.18% on the day, after rising as much as 8.8% during trading. The closing gain was worth about $2.4 billion in market value, and the rise briefly topped $3 billion at the intraday peak.

The rally lifted Take-Two’s market capitalisation from about $38.2 billion at Tuesday’s close to more than $40.5 billion during Wednesday’s session. Trading was unusually heavy, with around 12 million shares changing hands, roughly four times the stock’s recent daily average.

Take-Two finished Tuesday at $203.93 and opened Wednesday’s session at $212.64, already well above the previous close. Buyers pushed the stock to a high of $222.65 during the morning, before it eased in the afternoon to settle at $216.54. The day’s low of $210.50 still sat comfortably above Tuesday’s closing price.

The opening jump followed the review embargo, as the first GTA 6 reviews lifted Take-Two shares soon after the market opened in New York. Take-Two outpaced the wider market throughout the day, with the Nasdaq 100 tracking fund QQQ up only around 0.3% and the S&P 500 fund SPY slightly lower.

The gain also recovered much of a sharp slide earlier in the week. Take-Two had fallen about 10% over the two trading days before launch, as some investors sold ahead of the release. Even after Wednesday’s rally, the stock remains down around 14% for the year and well short of its 52 week high of about $266.

Early sales estimates gave investors the clearest reason to buy. Research firm Sensor Tower said GTA 6 had sold about 17.07 million units, worth around $1.65 billion, on launch day. That is more than double the $800 million GTA 5 made in its first 24 hours in 2013, which itself set records at the time.

title: Who Is Mandy in GTA 6? Jason’s Tenant, the Pipework Mission and Fan Theories

She appears early in the campaign, during one of Jason’s first jobs in the Leonida Keys. This article contains light spoilers for that Chapter 1 mission.

Mandy is a supporting character in GTA 6 and one of Brian Heder’s tenants in the Leonida Keys. Jason meets her in Pipework, the seventh story mission in Chapter 1, when Brian sends him to collect her overdue rent. She refuses to pay until someone fixes her clogged kitchen sink.

Her dialogue makes clear that she and Jason share a history, and she flirts with him throughout the scene. She also complains that Brian makes tenants pay through a website she describes as looking like it was “made by a fifth grader”. Rockstar Games has not named the actor who plays her or confirmed her age.

Jason arrives at Mandy’s home to find she has been washing dishes in the bathroom because the kitchen sink is blocked. He grabs a plunger and clears it himself, and Mandy then pays the rent. The scene also gives players a dialogue choice, letting Jason either provoke Mandy or defuse the conversation.

Pipework sits between Unwanted Attention and Hey Arnold! in the opening chapter, as the full GTA 6 chapters and missions list shows. title: Best GTA 6 Tips and Tricks for Beginners
content:
Grand Theft Auto VI changes more of the series’ core systems than any entry since GTA 5. Police remember what you wear, money can be lost on death, stats fade without training and completed story missions cannot be replayed. Players who carry old GTA habits into Leonida can lose cash, progress and hours of play.

These tips cover the systems that matter most in the first hours of the game, from saving and money to police, combat and character stats. They apply to both Jason and Lucia on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S.

GTA 6 has no mission replay menu, unlike GTA 5 and Red Dead Redemption 2. The only way to play a story mission again is to load a manual save made before it, and the game offers 15 manual save slots. Our guide on why you cannot replay missions in GTA 6 explains how to plan those slots across the campaign.

A good habit is to save at the start of each chapter and before each heist. With 93 story missions spread across five chapters, the GTA 6 chapters and missions list helps players see which missions are coming and where a save makes sense.

Players can lose a large share of the cash they carry if Jason or Lucia dies during free roam or a mission. Keep most of your money in the Floor Stash at a safe house, or deposit it at the bank. Banking opens after the Buck Me mission in Chapter 1, and Jason has a hiding spot under his bedroom floorboards from early in the game.

Police in GTA 6 work from the details they have on a suspect, including appearance, clothing and getaway vehicle. Wearing a disguise before a robbery and changing outfits afterwards makes escapes far easier. Switching cars once officers have identified your vehicle also helps break their search.

title: GTA 6 Lucia Trailer vs Final Game: Players Split Over Upgrade or Downgrade
content:
Grand Theft Auto VI players are sharing side by side comparisons of Lucia Caminos from the game’s first trailer and the finished game, and the images have split the community. Some players say Rockstar Games improved her character model before launch, while others argue she looked better in the 2023 reveal. The debate took off within hours of the game’s release on 19 November.

The comparison that spread most widely places two near identical shots of Lucia next to each other. Both show her in an orange prison uniform beside a chain link fence, lit by a low evening sun, in the scene that opened the first trailer.

The two images match in framing, pose and setting, which makes the differences in detail easy to spot. One version shows stronger contrast, with deeper shadows across her face and richer orange light on her skin. The other has softer, flatter lighting that shows more of her facial features, hairline and the background through the fence.

Her hair, face shape and expression also differ slightly between the two shots. Players have pointed to changes around her eyes, jaw and the way her hair falls, though the scene is otherwise the same moment from the story. It is the opening of the game’s prologue, which the GTA 6 missions list shows as Lucia’s first mission.

Players who see an upgrade point to the added detail in her skin and features, saying the final model looks more natural and closer to a real person. Others say the trailer’s heavier lighting made the shot more cinematic, and that the final scene looks flatter by comparison. Several players have argued the gap comes down to lighting and post processing rather than a new model.

Trailers are often rendered with settings tuned for a single shot, while the finished game has to run the same scene on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S in real time. Rockstar has not commented on the comparison or said whether Lucia’s model changed after the first trailer.

title: How to Increase Max Health in GTA 6
content:
Grand Theft Auto VI tracks three core stats for Jason and Lucia: Health, Stamina and Focus. Max Health decides how much damage either character can take in a firefight, and it grows only through one type of activity. Some popular habits, including running, do nothing for it.

The game also separates permanent gains from short boosts, so players who stop training can lose part of the progress they built. Knowing which activities feed which stat saves hours of wasted effort.

Max Health in GTA 6 increases through strength training with weight equipment. Bench presses, deadlifts and chest flys all count, and each completed workout adds to the character’s health bar. Players need enough stamina to finish a set, because a workout ends early if the stamina bar runs out.

Jason’s house in Shoeless Keys has gym equipment, which makes it the easiest place to train early in the story. Players also need to train regularly, because health and stamina gains fade if Jason and Lucia stop working out.

Running does not increase Max Health. Cardio activities such as running, cycling and kayaking build the Stamina bar instead, and they also burn calories. Players who want more health have to lift weights, while those who want to sprint for longer should focus on cardio.

Focus works differently from the other two stats. It controls how long Jason and Lucia can slow down time while aiming, which pairs with the reticle options in our guide on changing the crosshair in GTA 6 . Mindfulness activities such as fishing and pool raise Focus, and those gains are permanent. Players heading out to fish can use the GTA 6 wildlife guide to see what lives in Leonida’s waters.

title: GTA 6 Camera Guide: How to Take Selfies, Change Filters and Use Photo Mode
content:
Grand Theft Auto VI gives players two ways to capture Leonida: a camera app on Jason and Lucia’s in game phones and a full photo mode in the pause menu. The phone camera handles quick shots and selfies with poses and expressions, while photo mode offers detailed controls for lighting, focus and effects.

Neither tool is available from the first second of the game. Photo mode opens up during Lucia’s prologue, and the phone camera follows shortly after, once players take control of Jason.

The phone camera unlocks after Lucia’s prologue, when the story switches to Jason. The camera app sits on the phone’s home screen alongside apps such as Messages and Scooter Bros.

The rear camera includes a flash toggle, a 3×3 grid, zoom up to 5x and up to 17 filters. Photos can be viewed afterwards through the Gallery option inside the camera app.

Players switch to selfie mode by choosing the Selfie option in the camera app, which flips the view to the front camera. The selfie view adds three new controls on top of the photo and flash buttons.

Choosing Rear Camera switches the view back to normal photos. Jason and Lucia have separate phones, and the number of poses and expressions confirmed so far applies to Jason.

How to Change Weapon Crosshair in GTA 6
content:
Grand Theft Auto VI uses a three dash crosshair by default, which some players find harder to read than the single dot from GTA 5. Rockstar Games has included several reticle options in the game’s settings, covering the shape, size, visibility and hit markers.

The options sit inside the UI settings rather than the gameplay or controller menus, so they are easy to miss on a first look. The settings work the same way on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S.

The crosshair settings are listed under the Reticle section of the UI tab. Changes apply as soon as players close the menu, so they can test each shape and return to the settings if it does not suit them.

The Reticle section has six options. Reticle Shape decides the look of the crosshair, while the visibility sliders control how strongly it shows on screen when a weapon is held or aimed.

Complex is the default and changes shape depending on the equipped weapon. Simple and Dot use a smaller marker that stays the same across weapons, which is closer to the GTA 5 style. None removes the crosshair entirely, an option players can pair with a realistic aiming setup.

Hit markers add a brief signal on the crosshair when a shot lands, which helps confirm hits at long range. Turning them off gives a cleaner screen but removes that feedback. The two visibility sliders work separately, so players can keep the reticle faint while a weapon is simply held and make it stronger only when they aim down sights.

Huya Turns Its First Operating Profit Since 2022 as Game Publishing Outgrows Live Streaming
content:
Huya has posted its first operating profit in four years, as the Chinese game streaming platform leans harder on game publishing and in-game item sales to make up for a shrinking live streaming business. The NYSE-listed company reported operating income of RMB15.2 million (US$2.3 million) for the third quarter of 2026, against an operating loss of RMB14.3 million a year earlier. Acting chief executive Junhong Huang said operating income “turned positive for the first time since the third quarter of 2022”.

The results , released on 17 November for the quarter to 30 September, show a company in the middle of a shift. Total net revenues rose 3.8% to RMB1,752.8 million (US$261.4 million), but almost all of that growth came from outside live streaming. Net income attributable to Huya reached RMB29.3 million (US$4.4 million), up from RMB9.6 million in the same quarter last year.

Revenue from game-related services, advertising and other sources jumped 21.3% to RMB644.7 million (US$96.2 million), and Huya said the rise was driven mainly by in-game item sales and advertising. That line now makes up about 37% of total revenue, up from roughly 31% a year ago. Live streaming revenue, still the larger business, slipped to RMB1,108.2 million (US$165.3 million) from RMB1,156.7 million, a fall of about 4.2%. In money terms, the non-streaming business added RMB113.1 million year on year, while live streaming lost RMB48.5 million.

Huang pointed to game publishing as the main reason for the improvement. “Game publishing is becoming an increasingly important growth driver for our business,” he said, adding that Huya is advancing the release of The Legend of Swordman: Reunion and other titles. The company said it is drawing on what it learned from launching the mobile version of Goose Goose Duck. The release did not break out revenue for individual titles, and it did not give a launch date for The Legend of Swordman: Reunion.

The better revenue mix also helped Huya’s margins during the quarter. Gross profit rose 12.6% to RMB255.2 million (US$38.1 million), lifting gross margin to 14.6% from 13.4%. On a non-GAAP basis, operating income reached RMB30.5 million (US$4.6 million), which Huya said was its highest quarterly level since the third quarter of 2022. Non-GAAP net income attributable to Huya rose to RMB43.7 million (US$6.5 million), from RMB36.3 million a year earlier.

Huya said live streaming revenue “continued to stabilize” compared with the previous quarter, but it is still lower than a year ago. Huya built its business on game and esports live streaming in China, so the live streaming line remains the core of the platform. The Q3 release does not give monthly active user numbers, so it offers no direct read on whether its audience is growing. Live streaming still brought in about 63% of revenue in the quarter, down from about 69% a year earlier.

title: Oppenheimer Sets GTA 6’s Bar at 20 Million Copies in Three Days as Take-Two Stock Jumps 7%
content:
Oppenheimer has reiterated its Outperform rating on Take-Two Interactive with a $280 price target, and its launch-week note sets a clear bar for Grand Theft Auto VI. The broker expects about 20 million copies sold and at least $1.85 billion in gross revenue in the game’s first three days, according to a summary of the note published by Investing.com . Take-Two shares were trading at $218.92 at 12:53pm ET on Wednesday, up 7.35% on the day, according to Google Finance .

That price leaves about 28% of upside to Oppenheimer’s target. The stock had fallen almost 12% over the previous week, according to the same report, and our earlier analysis of the rebound covers how the reviews turned that around. Trading volume had reached 6.8 million shares by early afternoon, roughly double the stock’s average daily volume of 3.34 million. The shares opened at $212.64, dipped as low as $201.66 and climbed to an intraday high of $221.83, giving Take-Two a market value of about $40.9 billion.

The note lays out four markers that investors can check against the launch as it happens. Oppenheimer expected an aggregate Metacritic score of 97 or higher and a Twitch peak of about 2 million viewers. Its sales tests are around 20 million units in three days and gross revenue of $1.85 billion or more over the same period. It also flagged cyberattacks on console networks as the main launch-day risk.

Two of those tests have already been passed. GTA VI holds a 99 Metascore from 147 critic reviews, which our reviews roundup tracked as the embargo lifted, and that beats the 97 Oppenheimer set as its benchmark. On Twitch, the game’s category page passed 3 million concurrent viewers on 18 November, well above both the 2 million estimate and the 1.82 million peak the note cites for the gameplay reveal.

The sales tests will take longer to settle. Oppenheimer used a Sensor Tower estimate of 15.88 million pre-ordered units as a comparison point, and it said Take-Two could share its first sales figure as early as 20 November. A first-weekend update could follow on 23 November, which would give investors a direct read on the 20 million target.

Oppenheimer is not alone in staying bullish through the launch. After Take-Two’s second-quarter results earlier this month, DA Davidson kept a Buy rating with a $300 target, Piper Sandler held Overweight at $290 and BMO Capital stayed at Outperform with $285. TD Cowen kept its Buy rating at $284, while UBS cut its target from $300 to $295 and kept its Buy call. Our analysis earlier this week found an average TipRanks target of $290.50, close to where most of these brokers sit.

title: GTA 6 Streamers Are Getting YouTube Warnings Over In-Game Nudity: How to Avoid a Strike
content:
GTA 6 streamers on YouTube are reporting Community Guidelines warnings after in-game nudity appeared on their live broadcasts, and the timing could not be worse for anyone planning a launch marathon. Streamer Frag, who posts as @FragDempsey on X, shared a screenshot on 18 November showing his GTA 6 live stream removed under YouTube’s “Nudity and sexual content” policy. His advice to other creators was blunt: do not go into the game’s strip club while you are live.

DON’T GO IN THE STRIP CLUB IN GTA6 WHILE LIVE I GOT BANNED ON YOUTUBE LMAOOOO

A second warning seen by TalkEsport, for a stream titled “Grand Theft Auto 6 – Race to 100% Completion!”, cites the same policy and points to a moment 33 minutes and 30 seconds into the broadcast. Both notices are formal warnings, not channel bans, though Frag described his as a ban in his post. That difference matters, because a warning can turn into a strike, and a strike blocks live streaming for a week.

Grand Theft Auto VI is made for a mature audience, and its rating says so. The ESRB rates it M for Mature 17+ , and its content descriptors include Nudity and Strong Sexual Content alongside Intense Violence and Use of Drugs and Alcohol. A mature rating on the game does not change what YouTube allows on its own platform, though.

YouTube’s nudity and sexual content policy applies to live streams as well as uploaded videos, and it covers illustrated and animated content, including video games. It bans the depiction of clothed or unclothed genitals, breasts or buttocks that is meant for sexual gratification. Content with nudity that does not cross that line can be age-restricted instead, and YouTube weighs whether body parts are the focal point and whether the imagery is fleeting or prolonged.

Live streams make that line harder to manage. On an uploaded video, a creator can trim or blur a scene before anyone sees it, but on a live broadcast every second goes out unedited. Time spent inside a club venue in a game rated for nudity was enough for YouTube to remove Frag’s stream, according to his screenshot.

title: CS2 Adds Snowy Cobblestone and Fixed-Price Major Stickers
content:
Valve's Nov. 17 Counter-Strike 2 update brings Snowy Cobblestone to matchmaking, sells Singapore Major stickers at fixed prices and adds 8 music kits.

Valve's Nov. 17 update for Counter-Strike 2 brings Snowy Cobblestone to official matchmaking, returning the classic map after more than seven years. It also puts PGL Major Singapore stickers on sale at fixed prices and adds eight Monstercat music kits.

Valve announced the latest Counter-Strike 2 update at 6:38 p.m. ET in a Steam blog post titled "The Cobbled Road to Singapore" , and Dust2.us has a detailed breakdown of the changes. The map lands in Casual, Competitive, Wingman, Retakes and Deathmatch, while Boulder, Fachwerk and Shelter leave the official pool.

Cobblestone first appeared in the series in 2000 with Beta 6.5 and reached modern Counter-Strike in 2013 through the Winter Offensive update for Counter-Strike: Global Offensive , HLTV noted . It became a pro-scene staple and was the third most-played map in HLTV's database in 2016.

Valve pulled it from the Active Duty pool in 2018. A Halloween update that year changed the layout and landed badly with players, and the map left competitive matchmaking in 2019. Dust2.us said the new version drops the much-derided A-site changes from the final CS:GO edition.

The snowy version keeps landmarks such as Drop, Chicken Coop, Stables and B Long. Valve said in its blog post that the map has "undergone changes and features new pathways and locations for players to master."

title: G2 Esports x Umbro: Every Piece in the New Football Streetwear Collection and What It Costs
content:
G2 Esports has teamed up with Umbro on a limited-edition football streetwear collection, and the five-piece set went on sale on 18 November. The joint announcement from Berlin describes it as the start of a longer partnership, with more news planned for early 2027. Prices on G2’s store run from €30 for the beanie to €110 for the hooded track jacket, and the full set costs €360.

The collection pairs Umbro’s football terrace heritage with G2’s branding in a deep forest green, finished with chequered tartan details and woven patches. It is sold through the G2 shop and on Umbro’s UK site . G2 teased the drop on X a day earlier with the line “Your new Fall uniform”, before confirming it was available on launch day.

There are five items in the range, and G2’s store gives each one its own product page with a short description. Prices below are from G2’s store in euros, with the US price in brackets, and other regions see their own currency. The Hooded Track Jacket is the most expensive piece, and buying all five at the listed prices comes to €360, or $538 in the US.

The jacket and track pants are designed as a matching terrace set, and G2’s product pages point buyers from one to the other. The polo’s product page opens with the line “EST. 2015. STILL RUNNING THE PITCH.”, while the jacket’s page promises “terrace heritage” and a “villain mentality”. title: Epic Takes Legal Action Against a Rocket League Cheat Seller, Bans Them From Every Epic Game
content:
Epic Games says it has taken legal action against a seller of Rocket League cheats, and the seller is now permanently banned from every Epic game. According to the publisher, they published a note, under the “Update on our fight against cheating”, alongside a short apology video from the seller. Epic’s post was blunt about the reason, stating that selling cheats is against its rules.

The video, titled “An Apology to the Rocket League Community” and hosted on YouTube, is a plain text statement on a black background. “I sold cheats for Rocket League and that wasn’t fair,” the seller says in it, adding that cheating ruins matches for everyone. The statement ends by confirming they have stopped selling cheats and are banned from Rocket League and all other Epic Games products.

Epic has not said what form the legal action took. Its post does not mention a lawsuit, a court, a settlement or any payment, and it does not say how long the seller had been operating. What it does confirm is the outcome: the cheats are no longer for sale, the seller has apologised publicly, and the ban covers Epic’s whole catalogue instead of Rocket League alone.

That last point matters, because a ban across Epic Games products cuts the seller off from Fortnite, Rocket League, Fall Guys and anything else tied to an Epic account. Epic’s community rules tell players not to cheat, grief or exploit bugs, and not to promote or advertise known cheats. Selling them goes a step further, which is why Epic chose legal action in this case.

We are not naming the seller or the product here. TalkEsport does not publish the names of cheat sellers or cheat tools, even in enforcement stories, so readers are not pointed towards them. Epic named the seller in its own post on X, and the apology video is public on YouTube.

This is not the first time Epic has paired legal action with a public message. In July 2025, the Newsroom account said Epic had taken legal action against two people , one who sold and used cheats and another who carried out DDoS attacks on creators while they were livestreaming. Both were ordered to stop and banned from Epic’s games.

title: Krafton’s AI Horror Game MIMESIS Wins at the Korea Game Awards and Passes 2.4 Million Sales
content:
Krafton’s AI horror game MIMESIS has won an Excellence Award at the 2026 Korea Game Awards, and the publisher says the game has now sold more than 2.4 million copies worldwide. The co-op title from ReLU Games, a creative studio inside the BGMI and PUBG maker, picked up the prize at the ceremony at BEXCO in Busan on 18 November. Krafton’s announcement said judges rewarded the way the game builds artificial intelligence into its core design.

The Korea Game Awards are hosted by South Korea’s Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism and organised by the Korea Association of Game Industry. Winners are judged on artistry, technology and popularity, with an expert panel counting for half of the score and public and media votes for a quarter each. MIMESIS shared the Excellence Award tier with Supercat’s Dokkaebi’s World and Com2uS’s MMORPG Zeus, while all four technical and creative awards went to Crimson Desert.

The night belonged to Pearl Abyss, whose Crimson Desert took the Grand Prize as part of the record eight-award haul we covered earlier . Crimson Desert has sold more than 6 million copies since its March release, according to the ministry. NC’s Aion 2 won the Prime Minister’s Award, while Nimble Neuron, the developer of Eternal Return, received the Esports Development Award. Culture minister Choi Hwi-young also used the evening to back a tax credit for game development .

MIMESIS is a four-player co-op horror game built around monsters that copy the people playing it. According to Krafton, the AI-driven enemies imitate a player’s appearance, actions and voice, so the person standing next to you might not be your teammate at all. The AI also reads its surroundings and reacts to what players do, which keeps the group guessing about who is real.

Krafton describes it as an “AI-native game”, meaning the AI is the main source of the experience instead of a background system. That design is what the Korea Game Awards judges singled out, according to the publisher. It also fits Krafton’s wider bet on AI, which in India includes a $250 million commitment to AI and deep tech startups announced in September.

ReLU Games has kept updating the monsters since launch. In October, to mark a year in Early Access, the studio released its second major update, called OFF THE RAILS. It added a feature that copies players’ habits and a new Paranoia system, both aimed at making the imitations harder to spot.

title: LCS : Zven aussi attendu chez FlyQuest

title: SkewMond Joins Karmine Corp as G2 Lose Their Star Jungler
content:

SkewMond was not a free agent. G2 extended his deal in February 2026 and it was set to run until 2028, so the club had no reason to let him walk for nothing. Karmine Corp had to pay a transfer fee to get him out of that contract. The size of the fee has not been reported.

The two clubs settled the buyout on Tuesday, November 17, and SkewMond now has a verbal agreement in place with KC for next season.

Karmine Corp were not the only team chasing the French-Lebanese jungler. What slowed everything down was SkewMond himself. He wanted Karmine Corp, and that pushed talks into a standoff until G2 and KC agreed on a price.

This move has a strange echo. Two years ago, SkewMond took Yike's spot at G2 . Yike landed on his feet at Karmine Corp. Now Yike is reportedly off to Fnatic, and the player stepping into his old seat at KC is SkewMond, again.

title: LCK : Zeus de retour chez T1, deux ans après son départ ?

De son côté, Zeus a connu une année contrastée avec Hanwha Life, remportant notamment le MSI avant de subir une élimination dès le Swiss Stage des championnats du monde.

Si ce transfert se confirme, il marquerait surtout la réconciliation entre Zeus et T1. Pour rappel, le départ du joueur à l’automne 2024 avait provoqué une importante polémique autour des négociations contractuelles. T1 et l’agence du toplaner s’étaient publiquement opposées sur les circonstances de cette séparation, avant que l’organisation ne présente des excuses en 2025 concernant le harcèlement subi par le joueur et sa famille. Deux ans plus tard, les différentes parties sembleraient donc prêtes à tourner la page.

T1 préparerait également une réorganisation de son encadrement technique. Kim « Roach » Kang-hui, ancien entraîneur de l’équipe et double champion du monde en 2023 et 2024, serait pressenti pour revenir au poste de Head Coach après avoir terminé son service militaire. Avec un potentiel cinq majeur composé de Zeus, Oner, Faker, Peyz et Keria, la structure coréenne afficherait clairement ses ambitions pour 2027. Reste désormais à attendre une confirmation officielle de ce retour qui pourrait être l’un des transferts les plus marquants de l’intersaison.

title: GTA 6 Reviews Are In: 99 on Metacritic, Tying the Highest Score Ever
content:
The first Grand Theft Auto VI reviews are out, and critics have handed Rockstar Games something close to a clean sweep. The review embargo lifted at 11:00 UTC on 18 November, which was 4:30pm in India and the same moment the game unlocked in New Zealand, as our New Zealand release time guide set out. By 4:40pm Indian time, OpenCritic showed a Top Critic Average of 98 from 52 reviews, with 100% of critics recommending the game. Metacritic followed minutes later, and by 4:46pm GTA VI had a Metascore of 99 from 100 critic reviews. That ties The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time for the highest Metascore any game has ever received, and it beats the series record of 98 that GTA IV set in 2008.

Most of the early verdicts are perfect scores. Push Square, Screen Rant, DualShockers and the Korean outlet Inven all gave GTA VI 10 out of 10, while VGC, GamesRadar+, TechRadar, Giant Bomb, The Guardian and Digital Spy gave it five stars. The lowest scores in that first wave were Wccftech’s 9.6 out of 10 and ZTGD’s 9 out of 10, and Metacritic counted no mixed or negative reviews among its first 100.

The open world is the clearest point of agreement among reviewers. Push Square called it the deepest and densest open world since Red Dead Redemption 2, while GamesRadar+ described the game as “the highest-fidelity sandbox of its generation”. TechRadar and Inven both pointed to random events and unscripted moments that make Leonida feel alive between missions.

The two leads have landed well with critics too. VGC, Screen Rant and TechRadar all praised the chemistry between Jason and Lucia, and VGC ranked the pair among Rockstar’s best characters. The radio stations, soundtrack and sound design come up again and again, alongside the visual detail that VGC and TechRadar both single out.

Reviewers also highlight the new systems layered over the familiar GTA formula. Push Square praised the wanted system, the stealth options and a romance system, and Inven noted a heat-based police pursuit and a crime profile. Those match what Rockstar described before launch, when it said a criminal profile would track how violent each player is, as covered in our report on Rockstar’s empathy comments .

Performance is the most common complaint in the early reviews. GTA VI targets 30fps on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S, and Push Square found no 60fps or performance mode even on PS5 Pro, as our report on GTA 6’s 30fps target explained before launch. VGC noticed occasional slowdowns in the busiest areas but described them as rare, while TechRadar said players who cannot accept 30fps may want to wait for a PC version, which Rockstar has not announced.

title: New Zealand’s Tourism Board Invites GTA 6 Players to ‘Join Us’ and Play Early
content:
New Zealand’s official tourism body has joined the GTA 6 launch hype by inviting players who use the “New Zealand trick” to come and join its residents. Tourism New Zealand , the government agency that markets the country abroad, posted a 12-second reel on its Pure New Zealand Instagram account at 10:50am New Zealand time on 18 November. That was 3:20am in India, and roughly 13 hours before Grand Theft Auto VI was due to unlock in the country.

The caption jokes that “one perk of seeing the sun first” is “getting GTA 6 first too”, before adding a direct nod to players elsewhere. It continues: “We heard a few of you are trying the New Zealand trick to join us. We get it, and we’d love to have you.” The post is tagged #NZMustDo, #NZBucketList and #GTA6, which puts a holiday pitch in front of gamers during the biggest launch week of the year.

The clip opens on a drone shot of a swimmer floating in clear water at Kaiteriteri Beach in Nelson Tasman. The on-screen text reads “Life, because we’re getting GTA 6 first”, laid out like a menu option. By Wednesday afternoon in India, the reel had about 1,500 likes and 34 comments on an account with 1.2 million followers.

GTA VI does not unlock at one moment around the world. The game goes live at midnight local time on 19 November in each region, and New Zealand reaches that point first, at 11:00 UTC on 18 November. That is 4:30pm in India, 11am in London and 6am on the US East Coast, as our New Zealand release time guide sets out.

Every other region then follows in turn as midnight moves west. Australia unlocks two hours after New Zealand, India 7.5 hours after, the UK 13 hours after and the US East Coast 18 hours after, according to our GTA 6 release times for every region . Players who pre-loaded the game after Rockstar opened pre-loads on 10 November can start as soon as their own region goes live.

That head start is what Tourism New Zealand is joking about. For anyone in New Zealand, launch night arrives while much of the world is still at work or school. For players in the Americas, the gap is big enough that New Zealanders will have played for most of a day before the game unlocks at home.

title: Rockstar says it will kick GTA 6 spoilers trolls from its Discord as launch begins
content:
Rockstar Games has warned Grand Theft Auto VI players to be careful with spoilers as the game starts unlocking around the world. Anyone who spoils the story on purpose will be removed from its official Discord server. The warning went out to the server’s Announcements and Server Updates roles ahead of the first unlock on Wednesday. GTA VI goes live first in New Zealand at midnight local time, which is 4:30pm in India, before rolling west across the globe over the next day.

“Please be mindful of spoilers as Grand Theft Auto VI begins to launch across the globe,” Rockstar wrote. It added that it wants to ensure everyone experiences Jason and Lucia’s story for themselves. The post had drawn more than 11,000 emoji reactions in the server by Wednesday afternoon.

Rockstar said it will “publish some new GTAVI channels to the server very soon”. Story discussion will only be allowed in certain channels, and members are told to “always use spoiler tags when discussing major story moments”. On Discord, that means wrapping text in two pairs of vertical bars or typing /spoiler before a message, as Discord’s spoiler tag guide explains.

The penalty is aimed at deliberate spoilers rather than accidents. “Intentionally posting spoilers to troll other Discord members will result in your removal from the server,” Rockstar wrote, pointing members to an updated rules channel. The message signed off with “See you all in Leonida”, close to the line Rockstar posted on X when the game was a week away.

Rockstar’s wider rules go beyond its own Discord. Its policy on posting Rockstar material says videos showing “the ending of the game” or “any other big reveal in the story” will be taken down, along with edited compilations of cutscenes and plot dialogue. Cutscenes are allowed inside a longer playthrough or a narrated Let’s Play, but isolated videos of the game’s cinematics will be removed.

GTA VI is not launching at one moment worldwide. As our GTA 6 release times guide explains, it unlocks at 12am local time on 19 November in each region, starting in New Zealand at 11:00 UTC on 18 November. That gives players in Auckland a head start of several hours over most of Asia and close to a full day over the Americas.

Spread evenly, the refund works out at about 38 Elo per affected player. FACEIT have not said how it is split between players. Seen from the other side, the 11,626 banned accounts had taken close to 1,700 Elo each from their opponents on average.

The timing follows the same pattern as the summer. FACEIT’s previous big wave came on 27 July, a little over a week before Season 9 began on 5 August. This one lands three weeks before Season 10, which starts with a soft Elo reset and placement matches, so the refunded Elo is on players’ accounts before the reset.

title: Mythpat Joins YouTube’s 24-Hour GTA 6 Launch Livestream as India’s Fourth Creator
content:
Mythpat is heading to Vice City with the rest of YouTube. Mithilesh Patankar, one of India’s best-known gaming creators, has been selected for “Launch Day: YouTube’s 24 Hour GTA VI Livestream”, the round-the-clock broadcast YouTube is running with Rockstar Games for the release of Grand Theft Auto VI on November 19. According to a press note shared by his team, he is one of just four Indian creators picked for the event.

That puts him alongside Total Gaming, Payal Gaming and Sharkshe, the three Indian channels named in the creator line-up published last week, which we covered when YouTube revealed its 24-hour GTA 6 launch livestream . Mythpat did not appear on that published list, so his place comes from his team’s announcement rather than YouTube’s own roster. Either way, it gives Hindi-speaking audiences a fourth familiar face on what is shaping up to be the biggest single broadcast of the launch.

For Indian viewers, the timing works out well. YouTube’s main broadcast begins at 12 AM ET on November 19, which is 10:30 AM IST, and runs for a full 24 hours, taking it to roughly 10:30 AM IST on November 20. Before that, comedy collective RDCWorld hosts a pre-show at 11 PM ET on November 18, or 9:30 AM IST on November 19.

In other words, the whole event lands in daylight hours across India, a rare luxury for a global launch. If you are still working out when the game itself unlocks on your console, our guide to the GTA 6 release time in India has the details. The launch card Mythpat’s team shared carries the US start time for the broadcast.

His team has not said when his segment airs within the 24 hours. His YouTube channel and Instagram are the best places to catch the slot once it is announced. YouTube has not published a running order for individual creators either, so the simplest approach is to keep the main stream open and watch each creator’s own channels for slot announcements on the day.

Mythpat built his audience on unscripted, high-energy Hindi gameplay commentary, the kind of personality-led streaming that suits a launch-day marathon. His reach beyond India is already on record: he won the Streamy Award in the International category in 2021 , one of the clearest signs that Indian gaming creators were being noticed on a global stage.

title: Crimson Desert Sweeps the 2026 Korea Game Awards, Setting New Record With 8 Wins
content:
Pearl Abyss’s open-world action-adventure Crimson Desert was the big winner at the 2026 Korea Game Awards, sweeping its competition and setting a new record in history of the event. The ceremony, which took place on the 18th at BEXCO Exhibition Hall 2 in Busan earlier today, saw the Pearl Abyss title take home eight trophies, the most any game has won at the show.

Its victories included the top Presidential Award , the new Global Game Award , and all four technical and creative categories for sound , planning and scenario , character , and graphics . The two individual honors for Best Developer and Popular Voice Actor went to its team, with Cho Yong-hyeon receiving the Outstanding Developer Award, and Lee Hyun, who voices protagonist Kliff, winning the Popular Voice Actor Award.

Crimson Desert takes home 8 awards at the 2026 Korea Game Awards! Grand Prize Best Planning & Scenario Best Sound Best Graphics Best Character Design Global Game Award Best Developer – Jo Yong-hyun Popular Voice Actor With this achievement, Crimson… pic.twitter.com/XPddc4dj3M

The previous record in the Korea Game Awards was six wins from a single game, achieved by Mabinogi Heroes (2010), PlayerUnknown’s Battlegrounds (2017) and Black Desert Mobile (2018). Note that the Global Game Award was only introduced this year to recognize Korean games that have done well overseas, and Crimson Desert is its first winner.

The grand prize came from a field packed with strong competition. Twelve titles were nominated for the main awards, with winners decided by a mix of judges (50%), a public vote (25%), and a media vote (25%). NC’s Aion 2 , which was seen as the main rival, still got some recognition, earning the Popular Game Award and the Top Excellence Award.

“I sincerely feel honoured to be able to win the game grand prize once again following Black Desert Mobile.” Pearl Abyss CEO Heo Jin-young said at the ceremony, “Pearl Abyss has pushed ahead with the mindset that game developers should be at the centre of the company, to deliver fun and unforgettable experiences to users that did not exist before.”

title: GTA 6 Is Being Sold to India, Not Launched in It
content:
Grand Theft Auto VI unlocks in India at midnight, and Indian players have not been short of reminders. PlayStation India told its followers to start pre-loading on 10 November, the day pre-loads opened, and Rockstar has been running pre-order adverts that show up in Meta’s records for India. What India has not had is a launch built for it, the kind that Rockstar and Sony have staged in Korea, Japan and the United States.

Grand Theft Auto VI is the most pre-ordered game in PlayStation Store history! Mark the occasion with a video showcasing why GTAVI plays best on PS5. Get ready for launch on November 19 by clearing PS5 storage space and pre-loading today. #psindia pic.twitter.com/FidaYmtGne

That gap explains the frustration under PlayStation India’s latest post, a pre-load reminder on 18 November. One reply simply read “No marketing in india wow”, and another said the account “seems to be running in 2G era”. We went through PlayStation India’s posts, Meta’s advert records and Indian retail listings to see whether that complaint holds up.

The short answer is that GTA VI is being sold to India rather than launched in it. Indian players are seeing the same global adverts and trailers as everyone else, along with a fair rupee price. The local touches that other markets received, from celebrity films to menus in their own language, have not reached India.

PlayStation India has posted about GTA VI regularly since pre-orders opened. Its X account promoted pre-orders on 29 June, the limited-edition DualSense controllers on 3 September and Rockstar’s launch trailer on 15 October. In November it added the “most pre-ordered game in PlayStation Store history” video on the 10th, a one-week countdown on the 13th and the pre-load reminder on the 18th.

Instagram is where those posts travel furthest for PlayStation India. PlayStation India has about 886,000 followers there, compared with around 65,000 on X, and its 10 November video had about 52,800 likes by Wednesday. The caption told players to get ready by “clearing PS5 storage space and pre-loading today”, on the same day that Rockstar opened pre-loads , as our GTA 6 pre-load guide covered.

title: BGMI 4.7 Update: Arctic Chronicles, Erangel Subzero, Samay Raina Bus and Key Dates
content:
KRAFTON India rolled out the BGMI 4.7 update on 18 November, adding the Arctic Chronicles theme mode, a frozen Erangel Subzero map for Ranked and a Samay Raina collaboration. The final update of 2026 runs until 18 January and also launches the Popularity Battle Annual Gala, the Snow Festival and a New Year countdown event across most maps.

Arctic Chronicles is a Nordic winter theme mode on Erangel, Livik and Vikendi, live from 18 November to 18 January. Players can blow a horn to raise a submerged tower from its tail, or bind the beast at the Sealing Ground to earn Warrior Medals and a Pegasus.

The beast’s body also works as terrain. Squads can open caves inside it, break its shell for supplies, ride it as a moving platform and travel through it across Erangel. Eliminated players enter the Aurora Realm, where they chase starlight to earn a revival and parachute back into the match.

Arctic Chronicles adds Glyph passive skills including Aurora Blink, Tactical Shield and Air Drop Prediction. A new flying vehicle, the Aurora Pegasus, joins the mode as well.

Samay Raina is the third Indian creator to receive a BGMI collaboration, after CarryMinati in the 4.5 update and Techno Gamerz in 4.6. title: JioBLAST’s VCT South Asia Qualifier Goes BO3, Then BO1, Then BO3 Again, and Admins Say Riot Approved It
content:
Day two of JioBLAST’s VCT 2027 Kickoff Open Qualifiers for South Asia has brought a new complaint, this time about how long matches last. Indian Valorant coach Abhishek “GodspeedxD” Bajaj said on 18 November that after a best-of-three round of 128 the day before, teams would play the next two rounds as best-of-ones before switching back to best-of-threes. He added that the admins had told teams they had Riot’s approval for running the bracket this way.

PSA: Kickoff South Asian OQs will feature a probable first-in-history bracket featuring a bo3 ro128 bracket and then subsequent rounds with bo1s before returning to bo3s. Making teams play best-of-1s in the slot deciding qualifiers is a new low, and we havent yet truly started…

Bajaj did not hold back in his criticism of the decision. “Making teams play best-of-1s in the slot deciding qualifiers is a new low, and we havent yet truly started the season,” he wrote in his post on X . He called it “probably the first time in the history of esports” that earlier rounds were best-of-threes while later ones were best-of-ones, and said it was “just the tip of the iceberg”.

Neither JioBLAST nor Riot had responded publicly by Wednesday afternoon. The organiser’s X account has not posted about the qualifier since its reminder on 16 November, and TalkEsport has not seen the revised bracket published on any official channel. Without a published bracket, teams are relying on Discord updates and posts like Bajaj’s to follow the changes.

The difference between the two formats is bigger than it sounds. In a best-of-three, a team has to win two maps, so one bad veto, one hot opponent or one technical problem rarely ends its run. In a best-of-one, a single map decides the tie, which is why rounds that decide qualification are usually played as best-of-threes or longer.

The format also seems to have moved away from the one JioBLAST announced. As our guide to the South Asia Open Qualifiers explained, the 3 November announcement described a Swiss stage from 17 to 20 November, followed by a double-elimination playoff for the top eight. Bajaj and other community voices are describing numbered knockout rounds instead, including a round of 128.

title: LEC : Riot Games ouvre la porte à une petite révolution
content:
Le LEC pourrait connaître un changement majeur dans les prochaines années. Après avoir officialisé le format de la saison 2027, Artem Bykov, commissaire de la ligue européenne, a apporté plusieurs précisions sur les réseaux sociaux. Si toutes les rencontres continueront de se disputer en présentiel l’année prochaine, Riot Games n’exclut pas de passer partiellement à un format en ligne à partir de 2028. Une possibilité qui permettrait notamment d’envisager une saison régulière plus longue, avec davantage de confrontations entre les équipes.

« Avec notre organisation actuelle, nous ne pouvons pas raisonnablement mettre en place une saison régulière en double round robin sans matchs en ligne » , a expliqué Artem Bykov. Une telle évolution nécessiterait toutefois un important travail de préparation pour garantir la qualité des retransmissions et l’intégrité compétitive. « Jouer en ligne ou adopter un double round robin à l’avenir (2028 et au-delà) est une option que nous finirons par explorer, mais pour l’instant, notre priorité est de réussir 2027 » , a-t-il précisé. Aucune décision n’a donc encore été prise concernant cette éventuelle transformation.

En attendant, le LEC s’apprête à vivre une saison intense. Le Winter Split débutera le 15 janvier et s’étalera sur huit semaines, avec jusqu’à cinq jours de compétition par semaine durant la saison régulière. Les dix équipes s’affronteront exclusivement en Bo3, avant des playoffs réunissant les six meilleures formations en Bo5. Ce format sera conservé pour les trois segments de l’année, mettant définitivement fin aux rencontres en Bo1.

Tous les matchs se dérouleront à la Riot Games Arena de Berlin ou lors des Roadtrips organisés dans différentes villes européennes. Ces événements délocalisés continueront de se développer en 2027, avec de nouvelles équipes partenaires et de nouvelles destinations. En contrepartie, certaines journées disputées au studio berlinois ne seront pas ouvertes au public. Riot Games devrait dévoiler le calendrier complet du Winter Split à la mi-décembre, avec davantage de précisions sur les possibilités d’assister aux rencontres.

title: We Got a GTA 6 Game of the Year Nominee Before GTA 6
content:
For years, “we got X before GTA 6” was the internet’s favourite way of saying something would take forever. On 17 November, The Game Awards delivered the final version of the joke. Grand Theft Auto VI was named one of six Game of the Year nominees and picked up eight nominations in total, two days before the game goes on sale.

The reaction on social media was instant and loud. Under The Game Awards’ own post on X asking fans for the most surprising nomination, the top replies pointed at the game that “isn’t even playable yet”, and some called the show rigged. Our view is simpler: GTA VI broke no rule to get here, but the rules now produce a result that looks bad, and The Game Awards should fix that before next year.

The eligibility rule is a sales date, not a nominations date. According to The Game Awards’ FAQ , as quoted by Make Tech Easier, games had to be “commercially available to customers on or before Friday, November 20, 2026”, with a cut-off of 9pm Pacific time. GTA VI launches on 19 November on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S, which puts it inside the window with a day to spare.

That release date was not chosen to suit the show either. As our GTA 6 guide sets out, Rockstar first targeted 2025, then moved the game to 26 May 2026 and finally to 19 November. Had the last delay pushed it a few days further, GTA VI would have been a 2027 contender instead.

2 days Sources: The Game Awards, Rockstar Games, Insider Gaming. Graphic: TalkEsport The selection process is also harder to rig than the replies suggest. A jury of media and creator outlets, which our full list of The Game Awards 2026 nominees put at more than 160, submits unranked ballots, and the most-named games become nominees. The jury then decides 90% of each result, with the fan vote worth 10%, and the FAQ states that host Geoff Keighley does not vote.

The problem is timing, and it is hard to explain away. The shortlist went out on 17 November, while critic reviews are reportedly due on 18 November, a date Insider Gaming says it verified but Rockstar has not confirmed. That means the public saw GTA VI named a Game of the Year nominee before it could read a single published review.

Darren “iShowSpeed” Watkins Jr. just won Streamer of the Year at Esports Awards 2026.

On Nov. 17, content creator iShowSpeed won the Streamer of the Year title over 11 other nominees, including Kai “Kai Cenat” Carlo Cenat III, Case “CaseOh” Baker, Nicholas “Jynxzi” Stewart, Marc “Caedrel” Robert Lamont, Mark “OhnePixel” Zimmermann, and more.

Upon being named the Streamer of the Year, iShowSpeed went up on stage and talked about his victory.

“To be honest, I don’t even know what to say, but I just wanna first thank my fans. The only reason why I’m up here — every stream, every crazy moment, every country — you guys always show up and treat me like I’m one y’all and treat me like home,” iShowSpeed said.

He continued, thanking his team behind the cameras and his family before giving some advice to aspiring creators.

“Listen. I started streaming as a kid just with a camera and energy,” he said. “If any of y’all out there got a dream, just take that first step of doing it, you know? That’s all it takes. I love you all so much.”

title: Team Spirit sends Aurora Gaming to the lower bracket, claims first final spot at Dota 2 1w Essence 3
content:
In a series score of 2-0, Team Spirit quickly closed the curtain for Aurora Gaming as the three-time TI champs set their eyes on the grand final series of 1w Essence 3 , scheduled later today.

Team Spirit delivered an outstanding performance in the upper bracket final, comfortably defeating Aurora Gaming, a Tier 1 team that had fought its way into the top three. The victory made the matchup look like a walk in the park for Spirit.

The squad led by the now legendary carry player Illya “Yatoro” Mulyarchuk looked incredibly well on their way to the trophy, as they haven’t dropped a single game so far in the playoffs.

Despite facing a tougher path to the grand finals than Aurora Gaming, Team Spirit made quick work of their opponents. This included PARIVISION, who fought their way back through the lower bracket and are now set to face the recently defeated Aurora Gaming in the lower bracket final of 1w Essence 3.

Team Spirit’s performance against Aurora Gaming was reminiscent of Team Yandex’s playstyle. They consistently picked off isolated enemies, forcing Aurora to fight before its cores reached their power spikes. This approach worked particularly well against Aurora’s carry, Oliver “skiter” Lepko , who struggled to farm enough gold to make an impact in teamfights.

Bohdan “Batyuk” Batiuk, who is temporarily filling in for Magomed “Collapse” Khalilov during his extended break, has shown plenty of promise. The Team Spirit offlaner consistently outfarmed skiter while recording just three deaths across the first two games against Aurora Gaming. That’s an impressive showing for a stand-in offlaner and a sign of his potential.

title: Nekochuofficial interview: Finding a hero through Soldier: 76
content:
When Overwatch launched in 2016, players were introduced to 21 heroes. One of these heroes was none other than Soldier: 76, and even after 10 years, he remains a fan favorite. Esports.gg sat down with Soldier: 76 connoisseur Nekochuofficial to learn about what makes the hero so compelling even after all these years.

In his interview with esports.gg, Nekochuofficial shared that he first discovered Overwatch through his sister before finding a personal connection with Soldier: 76. Back in 2016, his sister started playing the game and showed him many of the cinematics.

Interestingly, however, she didn’t show him the “Hero” one featuring Soldier: 76. It was in 2021 when Nekochuofficial’s best friend introduced him to more of the Overwatch roster. This led him to duking it out as Reaper and learning more about his story before discovering his eventual favorite. Nekochuofficial really liked the Soldier: 24 skin that belonged to Reaper back then and even now.

“My best friend was showing me Overwatch characters around mid-to-late 2021,” he said. “I actually used to be a Reaper main before I became a Soldier: 76 main. I’ve been playing since before the Overwatch 2 stuff got around, but that’s where I think I really started.”

Speaking of Reaper, it was a piece of Reaper76 fanart that sparked Nekochuofficial’s interest in Soldier: 76. The artwork showed the characters in their younger days as Gabriel Reyes and Jack Morrison , and Nekochuofficial became a fan of the handsome Strike Commander.

Reading the “Bastet,” “Future’s Past,” and “Lucky Man” short stories then helped him appreciate Soldier: 76 beyond his appearance.

title: Valve’s wintry Cobblestone teaser brings back snax’s 1v4
content:
A 30-second clip of a snowed-in castle, a ten-year-old Sadokist call and three words of text: that is everything Valve have said about Cobblestone so far.

Valve posted a teaser for a snow-covered Cobblestone on the official Counter-Strike account at 19:17 CET on Tuesday, with the caption “‘Tis the season.” The 30-second video flies through the map’s courtyard under snow and ends on a red wax seal reading “Cobble”. No date, mode or patch note came with it.

'Tis the season. pic.twitter.com/qRLYkRHAmL

The sound under the footage is older than CS2. It is Matthew “Sadokist” Trivett commentating Janusz “snax” Pogorzelski ‘s 1v4 pistol clutch for Virtus.pro against NAVI at ESL One New York 2016. In the call, snax dances between the boxes with a USP and beats s1mple , GuardiaN and flamie in turn, until Sadokist asks: “What in God’s name is that from snax?”

s1mple , one of the three players snax beat in that round, answered Valve’s post with one word.

The round came on the biggest stage of that event. Virtus.pro and NAVI met in the grand final at Brooklyn’s Barclays Center on 2 October 2016, and Cobblestone was the first map. The Poles started on the T side, led 13-2 at the half and took the map 16-3. The USP in snax’s hand puts the clutch in the pistol round after the switch. NAVI still won the series 2-1 on Train and an overtime Mirage.

title: LEC : échec des négociations avec Solary, Shifters finalement maintenu en 2027 ?
content:
Solary ne devrait finalement pas débarquer en LEC en 2027. Selon les informations de Sheep Esports , la structure française aurait bien entamé des discussions avec Shifters pour récupérer temporairement sa place dans l’élite européenne de League of Legends. Mais les deux organisations ne seraient pas parvenues à trouver un accord. Un coup d’arrêt pour cette piste, alors que Shifters avait contacté plusieurs structures, notamment issues des ligues régionales européennes, afin d’étudier la possibilité de louer son slot.

La question financière aurait notamment représenté un obstacle majeur pour Solary. Son cofondateur Wakz avait récemment expliqué qu’une arrivée en LEC était « pas impossible, mais peu probable » , évoquant un investissement considérable. Selon ses estimations, le fonctionnement d’une équipe sur une saison coûterait environ un million d’euros, avec une marge de 300 000 euros. En ajoutant la location du slot, la facture totale pourrait grimper entre 2 et 5 millions d’euros. Un montant difficilement envisageable pour la structure tourangelle, qui avait déjà dû mobiliser 200 000 euros supplémentaires pour financer ses nouveaux locaux.

Face à cette situation, Shifters aurait décidé de reprendre les choses en main. Toujours selon Sheep Esports , son directeur général Mathieu Debonnaire aurait commencé à contacter des joueurs et leurs agents pour préparer la saison 2027. Le jungler français Sheo participerait également aux discussions autour du futur effectif, même si sa présence dans l’équipe n’est pas encore garantie. Tous les contrats des joueurs de la saison 2026 sont arrivés à expiration le 16 novembre.

Cette reprise des activités laisse donc penser que Shifters pourrait finalement conserver sa place en LEC, même si une location du slot reste théoriquement possible. L’organisation devra toutefois rattraper son retard sur un mercato déjà bien avancé, plusieurs concurrents ayant bouclé leur recrutement. Après une saison 2026 particulièrement difficile, conclue aux dernières places du championnat, Shifters pourrait ainsi repartir de zéro avec l’objectif de retrouver de la compétitivité en 2027.

title: The Game Awards 2026 Nominees: Full List of Every Category
content:
Grand Theft Auto VI leads The Game Awards 2026 nominees with eight nominations, including Game of the Year, after Geoff Keighley revealed the shortlist across all categories in a livestream on 17 November. Rockstar Games’ open world title earned its place two days before its own launch, with its release landing inside this year’s eligibility window by a single day.

CONTROL Resonant and Resident Evil Requiem follow with six nominations each, while Phantom Blade Zero has five. The ceremony takes place on 10 December 2026 at the Peacock Theater in Los Angeles, with Keighley hosting for the thirteenth time. A jury drawn from more than 160 media and creator outlets picked the nominees, and fans can vote now through the official The Game Awards website .

Six games are competing for the top prize this year. The shortlist mixes new releases, a returning Remedy franchise and Nintendo’s remake of one of the most celebrated games ever made.

Grand Theft Auto VI appears in Game of the Year, Best Game Direction, Best Narrative, Best Score and Music, Best Audio Design, Best Performance, Best Art Direction and Best Action/Adventure Game. The game will not be in players’ hands when voting opens, as millions prepare for GTA 6 launch day streams later this week. Games released on or before 20 November qualified this year, while Players’ Voice entries have until 30 November.

Capcom holds two of the five Best Game Direction slots through Pragmata and Resident Evil Requiem. The Blood of Dawnwalker, the debut game from Rebel Wolves and Bandai Namco, is the only Best Narrative nominee absent from the Game of the Year list. Rahul Kohli earns a Best Performance nomination for Saros, alongside Manni L. Perez for Grand Theft Auto VI.

Big Walk is the most nominated independent release, with four nominations across Games for Impact, Best Independent Game, Best Family Game and Best Multiplayer Game. EA Sports FC 27 and Forza Horizon 6 compete in Best Sports/Racing Game, while Riot Games’ 2XKO features in Best Fighting Game.
