title: BGMI Popularity Battle Annual Gala: Registration Dates, Nine Tiers and Rewards
content:
Krafton India is bringing a Popularity Battle Annual Gala to Battlegrounds Mobile India (BGMI) with the 4.7 update on 18 November. Registration opens on the same day and closes on 24 November. The main event runs from 25 November to 27 December, with a Team Popularity Battle to follow in December. The update also adds a redesigned Mode Selection screen and a seasonal reward event called Chicko’s Loot.

Popularity Battle is BGMI’s social ranking event, in which players compete for recognition within the game’s community. The Annual Gala is a larger version of the format. Krafton India announced the event in Bengaluru on 12 November. It said further ways to earn points will be revealed when the event goes live. It has not said whether the Team Popularity Battle will use the same tiers and rewards.

The Annual Gala has nine ranking tiers. The highest tier is limited to 3,000 players. Each round of the event counts towards a final stage called the Peak Battle, which decides the rewards. Players who reach the top tiers receive exclusive in game honours tied to their ranking. Krafton India has not listed the rewards for each tier.

The event also introduces a Starlight Grand Prize. Every registered player has a chance to win it, regardless of their final tier. Krafton India has not said how many Starlight Grand Prizes will be given out or what the prize includes.

Chicko’s Loot runs from 20 November to 21 January 2027. Players collect Lucky Eggs by playing different game modes or by receiving them as gifts from friends. The eggs can be exchanged for rewards in an event shop. A mini game built around the Lucky Eggs will be added in December.

The Mode Selection screen has been redesigned with two sections, Mine and Discover. Mine lists the modes a player uses most, while Discover shows modes they have not tried. The new screen will reach players in phases during the update rather than all at once.

title: The TenZ Gamble: Why T1’s 2027 Roster Could Struggle
content:
T1’s 2027 VALORANT roster is complete, but three questions hang over it before its first match: who plays which role, which language the team calls in, and whether it can finally win a VCT Pacific league stage. The club confirmed Tyson “TenZ” Ngo on 12 November, ending a retirement that began in September 2024. TenZ replied to the announcement with “I’m back”. Austin “crashies” Roberts had joined a day earlier, and Gustavo “Sacy” Rossi was named head coach on 13 November.

The expected starting five is Kim “stax” Gu-taek, Yu “BuZz” Byung-chul, Ham “iZu” Woo-joo, TenZ and crashies. So “sungmin” Seong-min, previously head coach of T1’s academy side, returns as coach. The team is expected to debut at Red Bull Home Ground in December.

T1 cleared most of its staff on 2 November. Head coach Kim “KDG” Dong-gun and assistant coach Lee “CheongGak” Il-ho left, along with players Meteor, Munchkin and DH. T1 credited KDG with taking the team to its first Champions playoffs. Sacy, a Champions and Masters winner as a player, has never coached a team before. Two new players and a new head coach will start their preparation at the same time.

TenZ built his reputation on duelists, but he moved to controller in his final season with Sentinels. Since retiring, he has played only two professional series, for Sentinels’ academy team in May 2025. stax played controller for T1 in 2026, iZu played initiator and BuZz was the primary duelist. crashies has played both initiator and sentinel.

That leaves two recent controller players for a role most compositions fill once. If TenZ plays controller, stax has to move to another role. If TenZ returns to duelist, he shares the role with BuZz. crashies is the most flexible of the five, and T1 has not said how it will split the roles.

TenZ and crashies are the first non Korean players on T1’s main roster since the team joined VCT Pacific. The squad has three Korean speakers and two English speakers, with a Brazilian head coach. Mixed Pacific teams usually call in English, and crashies has already played in North America and Europe. T1 has not said which language the team will use.

JD Gaming has made its first move of the offseason, and it could change who plays Duelist for the team in 2027. According to VLR.gg, JDG signed 18-year-old Liang "glacier" Zhekai from Wolves Esports, a rookie who led Wolves in average combat score (ACS) at VCT 2026 China Stage 2.

JD Gaming has made its first move of the offseason, and it could change who plays Duelist for the team in 2027. According to VLR.gg, JDG signed 18-year-old Liang "glacier" Zhekai from Wolves Esports, a rookie who led Wolves in average combat score (ACS) at VCT 2026 China Stage 2.

Fans of the scene can follow how rosters are shifting across the circuit in our Valorant coverage , including TenZ's return to competitive play with T1 and wo0t's move back to Turkey with FUT .

Glacier turned 18 this past March. He made his debut in 2024 and spent time with several PUG (pick-up group) teams in Taiwanese competitions before making the jump to VCT China with Wolves earlier this year. The 2026 season was his rookie campaign at that level.

On Wolves he was the primary Duelist, the role built around taking first contact and creating space for the rest of the team on attack. VLR.gg reports that he led Wolves in average combat score (ACS) during VCT 2026 China Stage 2. ACS is a per-round measure of damage and impact, so topping a roster in it points to a player who was producing even while his team struggled around him.

On Wolves he played alongside his cousin Spring, who has also left the team this offseason.

title: GTA 6’s Leonida’s Weather Teases Six New Screenshots, Shows How Wild Its Weather Gets
content:
The Weather Channel spent Monday afternoon, US time, forecasting a state that does not exist. Three days before Grand Theft Auto VI launches on 19 November, the American TV network posted a six-part forecast for Leonida, the fictional version of Florida where the game is set. Each post came with a new screenshot supplied by Rockstar Games, and the opening post had passed 5.2 million views on X by Tuesday evening in India.

title: Nvidia Board Creates National Security Committee as Washington Presses for Answers on China Chips
content:
Nvidia’s board has set up a new committee to watch over the company’s national security work and export controls, five days after Jensen Huang resigned as chief executive. The National Security and Export Control Oversight Committee was announced on 17 November, the same day Nvidia reports its third-quarter results, the first under interim chief executive Colette Kress. In its announcement , Nvidia said the new standing committee will be responsible for board-level oversight of “national security policies, export control compliance and global trade risk management”.

The NVIDIA Board of Directors has established the National Security and Export Control Oversight Committee. Read the release: https://t.co/uIeCqHURiI

The timing is hard to separate from the pressure building in Washington. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has demanded answers from Nvidia’s board within 10 days, as we reported when he called for a “dramatic shakeup” at the company. A day before the committee was announced, the Commerce and Justice departments said in a rare joint statement that they had been investigating the Singapore cloud company Megaspeed since 2024.

Director Suzanne Nora Johnson, a former vice chairman of Goldman Sachs, will chair the committee. The other two members are Stephen Neal, chairman emeritus and senior counsel at the law firm Cooley, and John O. Dabiri, a professor of aeronautics and mechanical engineering at Caltech. All three are listed on Nvidia’s board of directors page , which now names Harvey Jones as chair.

Judging by those biographies, none of the three comes from a national security or export control background. The board appears to know it, because the committee will hire “independent, outside experts” in law, national security and trade compliance to support its work. It will meet at least four times a year, including sessions with management and private sessions without them.

The change to reporting lines may matter more than the committee itself. Nvidia’s existing National Security Team and Global Trade Compliance Team will now report directly to the committee, as well as to Kress on day-to-day operations. That gives the board a direct line to the teams that handle export compliance, rather than hearing from them only through management.

title: Legacy CS2 Orgs Could Quit If They Miss Majors, Warns TechGirl, as Sticker Money Dries Up
content:
Counter-Strike’s biggest names could start walking away from the game if they keep missing Majors, according to presenter and podcaster Sam “TechGirl” Wright. Speaking on the latest episode of Feed the Trolls , her show with Duncan “Thorin” Shields, she said she thinks “a lot of these legacy orgs eventually pull out of Counter-Strike if they’re not making the Major”. The warning lands a week before the PGL Major Singapore begins on 24 November, with fnatic, NRG, paiN and TYLOO all missing from the 32-team field.

Wright’s point is about money as much as prestige. Since Valve rebuilt the Major sticker system in May, an organisation’s income from the biggest event of the season depends far more on how far it goes. Teams that do not qualify get nothing at all, and for clubs with large wage bills and few other reliable revenue streams, that gap is getting harder to absorb.

For years, Major stickers were sold in capsules, and organisations and players negotiated their own splits in their contracts. Valve scrapped capsules for the IEM Cologne Major in May 2026 and moved to a Major Shop, where fans buy the exact stickers they want with tokens. Half of all sales still go to the tournament organiser, the teams and the players. What changed is that Valve now sets each team’s royalty rate by its seeding before the Major and its final placing after it, as Counter-Strike’s official account announced at the time.

The gap between the top and bottom of that scale is wide. The Major champion receives 2.85% of token sales, while the bottom-placed teams receive 0.72%, and each team’s share is now split evenly between the organisation and its five players. On every $100 million of sales, that leaves a champion’s organisation with about $1.43 million and a first-stage casualty’s with about $360,000. At Cologne, the bottom rate went to Gaimin Gladiators and SINNERS, whose organisations each took just 0.36%.

Some team owners warned about this months ago. M80 chief executive Marco Mereu said in June that the change “could cause teams to refocus on other events besides the Majors” as they look for income. Reports since then have described sales slowing sharply after the Cologne launch, and Valve skipped its usual end-of-event sticker sale for the first time. For organisations that relied on a healthy sticker cheque even after an early exit, the budget maths has changed, and missing the Major altogether now leaves an even bigger gap against rivals who go deep.

Wright also took aim at one organiser in particular. On the podcast, she said that “apparently” the chief executive of FiReSPORTS had claimed the sticker situation would be fixed after Singapore. “How convenient that leads into his Majors,” she added. FiReSPORTS , the Argentine company behind FiReLEAGUE, will host the first Major of 2027 in Buenos Aires, before Perfect World stages the second in Shanghai.

title: IEM Beijing locked in through 2028 as EFG signs 3-year deal with city esports body
content:
Under a three-year framework deal that ESL FACEIT Group (EFG) concluded with the Beijing Esports Industry Development Association, Intel Extreme Masters (IEM) Beijing will be held each year as a Counter-Strike 2 (CS2) tournament between 2026 and 2028. The deal was rubber stamped at a ceremony during IEM Beijing 2026, Insider Gaming detailed.

The Bloomage Biotech Biohyalux ECM Arena in Wukesong, Haidian District, successfully hosted IEM Beijing 2026 earlier this month, which MOUZ won. The Association, which is supervised by the Beijing Municipal Bureau of Press and Publication, will now start working closely with EFG and local authorities on a long-term support structure. The aim is for broadcasters, sponsors, and Chinese esports clubs to get the commercial safety net they crave.

Marc Winther, Director of Esports Counter-Strike 2 at EFG, hailed the deal as a flagship event for domestic fans. He also said the arrangement offers teams and partners in the area a stable footing for expansion.

Looking at the figures, it’s no surprise that EFG wanted to hang around: the 2026 edition prompted almost 60,000 fans to turn up across six days of competition, which EFG calls the biggest standalone IEM held in Asia ever . It also revived IEM's 360-degree arena stage for the first time since 2022, when the IEM Rio Major took place.

The commitment follows a run of strong domestic numbers. IEM's standalone Chinese debut was in Beijing in 2019. IEM Chengdu in 2025 sold out with more than 35,000 attendees and 770,000 peak online viewers. Research firm Niko Partners estimates CS2 pulled 137.5 million viewers on Chinese livestreaming platforms in June 2026, up 50 percent month on month, making it the second most-watched shooter in the territory.

Three years of municipal backing is a different proposition entirely from a one-off stop. Teams and sponsors now have a known destination they can plan around, while local fans are guaranteed top tier for the next three years at least. The 2026 edition has set a high bar for the next two.

title: PS5 Hacker Gezine Claims Game Dump on Firmware 14.22, the Version GTA 6 Reportedly Needs
content:
PlayStation 5 security researcher Gezine has claimed to have dumped a game executable on PS5 system software 14.22. Grand Theft Auto VI reportedly needs that firmware version to run, and the game launches on 19 November. Gezine announced the result on X but did not name the game. He has not shared his method, published any files or released a tool.

A game executable, also called a game binary, is the program code a game needs to run. The PS5 keeps that code encrypted and protected. Dumping it means copying the code out of the console in a readable form. It is one step in examining how a game works, but it does not amount to a full jailbreak of the console.

Gezine had previously said the established method for dumping games stopped working on firmware 14.00 and later. On 19 October he posted that the “old way to dump executables does not seem to work at 14.xx”. He suggested at the time that a hypervisor exploit might be needed. The new claim suggests he has found another route, although he has not explained it.

In late October, Gezine also shared screenshots that appeared to show access to the debug menu on firmware 14.10. Sony released firmware 14.22 on 2 November. Public exploit tools still stop at firmware 13.60, and no public jailbreak exists for any 14.xx version. On 13 November, another modder, Echo Stretch, warned players not to expect a pirated copy of GTA 6.

A dumped executable is also what emulator developers and modders study when they try to run console games on other hardware. Even so, a single dump on one console does not let other players copy or run games. Running a dumped game on a PS5 would still need a working jailbreak on the same firmware, and none has been shown for 14.22. Gezine has not said whether he plans to go further.

Gezine is known in the console homebrew scene for keeping his findings to himself. He reports vulnerabilities to companies through bug bounty programmes instead of releasing them publicly. He has found security flaws in both Nintendo and PlayStation consoles. That approach means a public tool based on this work may never appear.

Avec OpTic Gaming, les LCS récupèrent donc une marque emblématique de l’esport nord-américain. title: Paper Rex’s something Reportedly Cleared as a Pacific Resident, Freeing an Import Slot
content:
Paper Rex may have found the roster loophole every VCT Pacific team wanted. Riot Games has granted Ilia “something” Petrov an exception that lets him count as a Pacific resident in 2027, according to a report by Lion Esports on 16 November. The Russian duelist joined the Singapore club from Japan’s Sengoku Gaming in March 2023. If that holds, something would no longer take up one of Paper Rex’s two import slots, and the club could add a foreign player without breaking up its core. Riot and Paper Rex have not confirmed the ruling, although the club’s X account did little to cool the speculation the next morning.

Robert Pattinson to play under PRX for VCT 2027 pic.twitter.com/p19yPGsqWu

Lion Esports, citing sources close to the matter, said the decision also covers other long-serving Russian players in the region, naming Maksim “Jemkin” Batorov. It added that Riot had not said publicly what threshold it used, whether that was years of residency, years under contract in Asia or a case-by-case review. That gap matters, because the 2027 rules give Riot wide discretion here, and the timing comes weeks after Paper Rex lost Jinggg and d4v41.

The answer sits in Riot’s VCT Global Policies for 2027 , last updated on 28 September. Article 96 says a player can count as a resident of a region if they are a citizen, a lawful permanent resident or hold another special status such as refugee status. The fourth route is the one that matters here, because it covers a player who “was granted an exception to be considered a Resident”, which Riot may accept or reject at its discretion. There is no fixed number of years in the rulebook, so a case like something’s depends entirely on Riot’s judgement.

Article 108 then sets the hard limit on imports. Every team must field at least three residents of its home region in its starting five, which means a maximum of two non-residents. Articles 109 to 112 add a softer route for teams that kept their partnership, such as Paper Rex. These legacy exceptions let a starting lineup carry more than two non-residents, but only if every one of those players holds an exception, and each one ends when that player’s contract with the club expires.

That is why a residency exception is worth far more than a legacy one. A legacy exception protects a player only for the length of his deal and only alongside other protected players. A residency exception, if Riot has granted it, removes something from the import count altogether, so Paper Rex could sign two new non-residents around him instead of none.

title: Microsoft’s 24-Hour Outage Cost Customers About $9 Billion. Microsoft Pays a Fraction
content:
For almost 24 hours last week, much of the working world could not open its email. Microsoft’s preliminary incident report puts the Microsoft 365 outage at 23 hours and 50 minutes, from 16:20 UTC on 12 November to 16:10 UTC the next day, with Outlook and Exchange Online hit hardest. By TalkEsport’s estimate, it cost Microsoft’s customers around the world about $9 billion in lost working time, within a plausible range of $2 billion to $27 billion. Microsoft’s own maximum exposure, through the service credits it promises when it misses its uptime target, is less than a billion dollars, and its share price rose on both days of the outage.

That gap is the real story of the outage. The failure was Microsoft’s, the evidence in its own report suggests it was preventable, and yet nearly all of the cost landed on the companies, hospitals, schools and governments that pay for Microsoft 365. We built a simple model to put a number on it, and every step is shown below so readers can swap in any assumption they disagree with.

Microsoft has been unusually candid about the cause. Its preliminary post-incident report , dated 15 November and shared with administrators under incident IDs EX1550543 and MO1550821, describes a fix it built for the networking gateway that sits in front of many Microsoft 365 services. That fix carried a hidden defect, and it went live across the world from July onwards. For more than three months, it ran without causing any visible problem.

The defect was lock contention inside an internal Windows process, which meant tasks on the gateway servers waited on each other until processor time and memory ran out. Microsoft’s report admits that its load tests “tended to focus on weaker hardware with fewer cores”, while the bug got worse on newer machines with more cores. On 12 November, a routine Teams failover added load to the same gateway, nearly 14% of its capacity was already offline for an unrelated reason, and US peak traffic did the rest. As we reported while Outlook and Teams were still down , Microsoft spent most of the first night restarting servers that kept failing again.

The report’s own words explain why this one lasted so long. Automated traffic management moved users to healthy servers, which then hit the same bug, and “at its lowest, more than 80% of servers were unresponsive”. Because the faulty change was months old, Microsoft said its “normal rollback, flighting, and feature flags were unable to quickly revert the change”. Engineers had to build a new update instead, and it did not reach the first servers until 07:20 UTC on 13 November, 15 hours after the outage began.

While we're working to mitigate impact, we've confirmed the issue may affect Microsoft 365 service connectivity for users in any region, more information will be provided in the Microsoft 365 admin center under EX1550543.

title: US Breaks Silence on Megaspeed: Probe Began in 2024, Nvidia Cut It Off in June 2025
content:
The US government has broken its silence on Megaspeed, and its account puts Nvidia’s own role in a new light. In a rare joint statement dated 16 November, the Department of Commerce and the Department of Justice said they had been investigating the Singapore company since 2024. They also said Nvidia placed Megaspeed on its “no sell” list in June 2025, after Commerce investigators asked the chipmaker for records of its sales. The criminal case is now led by the Justice Department, and the two agencies promised to bring “the full extent of the law” against Megaspeed for any crimes it may have committed.

The agencies said they were speaking because of “inaccurate information circulating in public reporting”, although they did not say which reports they meant. Megaspeed is the cloud company whose former chief executive, Alice Huang, is at the centre of the scandal that ended Jensen Huang’s 33 years as Nvidia’s chief executive on 12 November. No charges against Megaspeed or Alice Huang have been announced, and Megaspeed has denied diverting Nvidia chips to China.

The statement sets out the clearest official timeline yet. According to the two departments, Commerce opened its investigation in 2024 “after identifying suspicious activity through proactive monitoring” of possible chip diversion. In May 2025, its investigators asked Nvidia for records of any direct or indirect sales to Megaspeed, and in June 2025 Nvidia added Megaspeed to its “no sell” list. That same month, agents from the Bureau of Industry and Security carried out an on-site end-use check at Megaspeed with Singaporean law enforcement officers. They also interviewed Alice Huang, whom the statement describes as the company’s chief executive.

An end-use check is one of the US government’s main tools for confirming that exported technology is where its buyer says it is, and is being used for the purpose declared. Doing one in person, alongside another country’s police, is a sign that investigators were already treating the case seriously by mid-2025. According to the statement, it was only “following this enforcement action” that the Justice Department took the lead in a criminal investigation, with Commerce’s export enforcement agents still working the case alongside federal prosecutors.

The statement also doubles as a defence of the government’s record. It credits Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, whom Senator Tom Cotton had urged to investigate Megaspeed , and Attorney General Todd Blanche. It also says 17 defendants in six separate investigations have been charged under the Trump administration over alleged smuggling of semiconductors worth billions of dollars. Commerce adds that its export control penalties are now 18 times higher than under the Biden administration. One of those prosecutions is a Southern District of New York case against three people accused of diverting US AI technology to China.

The timing makes the target of the statement fairly clear. On 9 November, The New York Times reported that the Commerce investigation was handed to the Justice Department after Nvidia’s general counsel, Tim Teter, contacted investigators in August 2025. The Times said Teter told investigators that Jeffrey Kessler, the Commerce under secretary who oversees export controls, had given him permission to reach out. Some agents reportedly worried that the contact could taint the case, and the Times said Commerce paused its own work at the Justice Department’s request.

title: GTA 6 Has Already Made $1.5 Billion, and Nobody Has Played It Yet
content:
GTA 6 is not out yet, and it has already pulled in about $1.5 billion. Sensor Tower's tracker counts close to 15 million pre-orders on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S with three days to go.

Sensor Tower's live tracker now shows $1.45 billion in revenue and 14.94 million copies sold for GTA 6 as of November 16. That covers PS5 and Xbox Series X|S only, across the Standard and Ultimate Editions. Round it up and you get 15 million copies and roughly $1.5 billion, with the game not out until November 19.

These are estimates. Rockstar and Take-Two have not published a pre-order total, and tracker figures can miss sales or count some twice, so treat the exact numbers with care.

The jump is the real story. When we last checked the tracker , it counted 9.69 million pre-orders and about $942 million. Since then it has added around 5.25 million copies and roughly $508 million. That is about a million extra copies every day.

Our own math on the new totals gives about $97 per copy. The base game lists at $79.99 on Amazon, so a lot of that money is likely coming from buyers who picked the pricier Ultimate Edition.

The latest split is 74% PS5 and 26% Xbox Series X|S. PlayStation alone has brought in just over a billion dollars. Xbox is holding a bigger share than many expected, and it has crept up a point since our last report.

title: Call of Duty Ranked Levels: Every Skill Division and What Carries Into a New Title
content:
Call of Duty ranked levels in mainline multiplayer Ranked Play run from Bronze to a Top 250 leaderboard finish. Black Ops 7 treats a new season differently depending on whether you finished below Platinum, and a new title begins its own progression. Warzone and Call of Duty Mobile have separate ranked systems.

Black Ops 7 Ranked Play has seven named Skill Divisions that group players by rank, followed by Top 250, a place on the leaderboard for the highest-ranked competitors. In order, the eight ladder positions are Bronze, Silver, Gold, Platinum, Diamond, Crimson, Iridescent, and Top 250. Top 250 is a leaderboard position rather than another ordinary division to grind through. As a new player, you’ll receive a starting rank only after winning the required placement matches.

This is the Black Ops 7 multiplayer ladder; Warzone and Call of Duty Mobile use their own ranked systems.

Players in the Bronze division through Gold keep their rank and SR when a new season starts, but players in Platinum and above need a placement win. Rank is only part of what a profile carries, though: building one from scratch with the level, weapons, and camos you want takes a long run of matches. Players who would rather start from a finished profile can browse Call of Duty accounts on Skycoach , a marketplace where each Black Ops 7, Modern Warfare 4, or Warzone account listing shows whether it is ranked-ready, along with its level, Prestige, camo count, weapons, and the platforms it links to (PC, PlayStation, or Xbox). Skycoach has operated since 2020, and purchases come with buyer protection: a warranty period, a refund policy, and 24/7 support.

Black Ops 7 starts with placements. You must win three placement matches to receive a starting rank, and after each placement win, the Minimum Starting Rank updates to show a projection of where you’re expected to land.

After a Ranked Play win, you gain Skill Rating (SR), which sets your position on the ladder. The amount isn’t fixed: it depends on your match performance relative to the skill of the other players and the team’s margin of victory. The same factors affect SR deducted after a loss. As Activision’s ranked support page explains, the SR change depends on these match factors, so two wins during the same evening can award different amounts without an error in the display.

title: GTA 6 Pre-Loads Just Broke Virgin Media’s Broadband Records, Beating Arsenal and Fortnite
content:
GTA 6 pre-loads gave Virgin Media its busiest day on record, eight days before the game is even out. In a press release on 11 November , Virgin Media O2 said its UK broadband network set new highs for both peak traffic and total daily data on Tuesday 10 November. Peak traffic beat the previous record, set during Arsenal’s Champions League semi-final against Atlético Madrid, by 3.8%. Total data for the day was 4% higher than the previous best, which was set only on 1 November by the launch of Fortnite’s Chapter 7 Mini Season.

The rush started as soon as downloads opened. Between midnight and 1am UK time on 10 November, which is also midnight to 1am UTC in winter, Virgin Media recorded a 51.6% rise in broadband traffic compared with the same hour a week earlier. By 9am, the total data downloaded was 73.3% higher than over the same period on Tuesday 3 November. At 23:05 UTC, the network passed its previous record for an entire day’s data, with almost an hour of Tuesday still to go. Virgin Media O2 did not say how many customers pre-loaded the game, or publish its peak traffic in terabits per second.

Grand Theft Auto VI pre-loading is now available for everyone who has pre-ordered. If you still have yet to pre-order, now’s the time to make sure you're prepared for November 19: https://t.co/LUoPLobocD pic.twitter.com/TLtJUSFBwN

Virgin Media puts the game at 190GB, slightly less than the 212GB of free space we reported in our GTA 6 pre-load guide . The company says customers on its fastest Gig2 broadband service can download it in under 15 minutes. Our own calculation, at full line speed with no overheads, gives just under 13 minutes on a 2Gbps connection. On a 100Mbps line, the same download would take more than four hours, so many players will want to start well before launch day.

Pre-loading was always likely to strain networks, given how many people have already bought the game. GTA 6 has become the most pre-ordered game on record, with an estimated 9.69 million pre-orders, according to Sensor Tower. Rockstar’s own pre-load announcement also confirmed that the game targets 30 frames per second on consoles, which has caused a backlash among players . That debate has done little to slow the downloads, judging by Virgin Media’s figures.

Virgin Media O2 also published polling from Strand Partners, a member of the British Polling Council , which surveyed 520 UK adults who expect to play the game on 30 October. Nearly half (46%) said they expect to download GTA 6 before release day, and 45% expect to spend at least £50 on gaming kit, not counting the game. More than three-quarters (78%) have changed, or plan to change, their schedules to find time to play. Almost a quarter (23%) expect to stay up later or sleep less, and 22% plan to keep a whole weekend free.

title: Best Permanent Unlocks to spend Tokens on in Modern Warfare 4
content:
Classic Prestige has returned in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4, and that means that Permanent Unlock Tokens are coming back as well. If you’re unfamiliar with how Prestige Mode works, it resets your level back to one, but you receive a Permanent Unlock Token that you can use on any class item in multiplayer in exchange.

This is a huge benefit, as it lets you permanently unlock an item so you never have to unlock it again during the entire Prestige grind in Modern Warfare 4 . However, with so many items to choose from, which unlock gives you the best bang for your buck?

Below, we’ll give you five distinct class items in MW4 multiplayer that are most worth spending a Permanent Unlock Token on after you Prestige. The item list is in order from 1-5.

First on the list has to be the Stim, which is a piece of Tactical Equipment that quickly heals you back to full health when applied. The Stim is unlocked at level 47 in MW4 multiplayer, making it one of the final items you’ll unlock every single Prestige.

While there are other solid pieces of Tactical Equipment you can use until that level, once you get used to the Stim, there’s really no going back. The ability to get back into the fight instantly after being injured, compared to waiting for several seconds to recoup health, is one of the most important benefits of any item in multiplayer. If you use a Permanent Unlock Token on the Stim, your Tactical slot is pretty much set in stone on all loadouts in multiplayer.

Next up, we have the Axion assault rifle, which is unlocked at level 52. The Axion is one of the best assault rifles in Modern Warfare 4, and having it available for only three levels every Prestige is ultimately a waste of its potential. This is arguably a top meta weapon in multiplayer, so you’ll want it permanently unlocked as soon as possible.

title: FaZe Clan’s 11.11.26 Teaser Is a $100,000 Call of Duty Tournament: What We Know About FaZe’s Return
content:
FaZe Clan’s cryptic “11.11.26” post now has its first answer: a $100,000 Call of Duty tournament. A few hours after the date appeared on FaZe’s X account on 9 November, the organisation released a trailer for the Flank Invitational, a two-day event on 11 and 12 November. It will be streamed on FaZe’s Twitch channel and on the channel of former Call of Duty pro ZooMaa. The teaser, FaZe’s first original post since March, had passed 600,000 views by Tuesday, and the account’s bio now reads only “11.11.26”.

ZooMaa’s tournament brand, The Flank, confirmed the details in a post on X headed “FAZE X THE FLANK”. It listed a “12 team fantasy draft” on 10 November, followed by the tournament itself on 11 and 12 November. ZooMaa, who still goes by FaZe ZooMaa on X, thanked “the team at @FaZeClan for getting this done” and said the teams would be drafted on Tuesday. FaZe has not said whether the tournament is the whole announcement, or the start of something bigger.

FaZe’s 41-second trailer opens with the words “FaZe Clan presents” over Call of Duty gameplay, and closes on a card reading “$100K Flank Invitational, November 11-12”. In between, it promises a double-elimination bracket across three modes: Hardpoint, Search and Destroy and Hijack. The maps shown carry the Korean street signs of Modern Warfare 4, the current Call of Duty, whose launch patch notes landed in October. No team list, player list or prize split had been published by Tuesday morning, India time.

The fantasy draft format has a history at The Flank. The Flank has run invitationals for Call of Duty League players since 2024, when ZooMaa announced a $100,000 series of Black Ops 6 events for pros. Its last edition, a $20,000 tournament in November 2025, was won by a four-player squad that included CDL player Dashy. In October, ZooMaa said in a clip shared by the account SpawnUp that this year’s event was “not even full teams bc they wouldn’t let me do it, again”, without naming who had blocked full rosters.

The teaser lands almost a year after FaZe’s creator side fell apart. In the last week of 2025, Adapt, JasonTheWeen, Lacy, Silky and Stable Ronaldo announced they were leaving, and FaZe veterans including Apex, Swagg and Rug followed. Bloomberg reported that Matt Kalish, the DraftKings co-founder who invested in FaZe Media in 2024, had asked creators to sign with his new agency, HardScope, or go independent, calling the old model “unsustainable”. On 28 December, FaZe said it was “heartbreaking to see this era of FaZe come to a close”, and that esports would become “our main focus moving forward”.

The main account has been close to silent since then, apart from a $10,000 Modern Warfare 2 trickshot challenge in March. Several of the departed creators moved on together, with Adapt, Silky, JasonTheWeen, Lacy, Marlon and Stable Ronaldo launching a new group, CORE, on 30 April. Co-founder Richard “Banks” Bengtson, who rebooted FaZe in 2024 before stepping down as chief executive in July 2025, replied to the teaser within an hour. “Although I have no part in whatever’s next for this brand, I will always root for its success,” he wrote , adding: “Thank you for changing my life.”

title: Call of Duty Chat Over FaceTime Sparks Bomb Scare and Evacuation at California’s Ontario Airport
content:
A Frontier Airlines plane and part of a terminal at California’s Ontario International Airport were evacuated on Sunday night, after a passenger mistook a man’s Call of Duty chat for a bomb threat. The man had been talking to a friend over FaceTime while the friend played the game, and another passenger heard him mention a bomb. A sweep of the aircraft found no explosive device, and police concluded that no crime had been committed, according to reports. The scare has since become one of the most shared gaming stories on X, where it reached the platform’s Today’s News section.

The incident took place at around 10pm local time on Sunday, 8 November, as the Frontier flight was preparing to depart. According to CBS Los Angeles , a passenger waiting on board heard someone say the words “bomb” and “explosion” and reported it to the crew. The California Post , which spoke to the Ontario Police Department, reported that the passenger heard the man say that “he had a bomb in his backpack”. Neither outlet reported the flight number or where the plane was heading.

Officers detained the man for questioning and confirmed that he was carrying a backpack, police spokesperson Denyse Quezada told the California Post. Passengers were taken off the plane, and the east side of Terminal 2 was cleared while flights were held. A bomb-sniffing dog team searched the aircraft and the surrounding area and found nothing dangerous, according to the same report. The Ontario Fire Department and a bomb squad also responded within minutes.

The man told investigators he had been on FaceTime with a friend who was playing the game online. “The friend was playing a video game called ‘Call of Duty,'” Quezada said, adding that “the subject’s statement was related to a video game and not an actual explosive”. Investigators contacted the friend, who backed up his account, and the man was released. Airport spokesperson Steve Lambert later said the investigation was complete and that operations at Ontario International Airport were resuming.

Reports differ on what happened to the man after he was cleared. CBS Los Angeles reported that all passengers, “including the detained individual”, got back on the plane for departure. The California Post said that everyone except the man was allowed to reboard. The Ontario Police Department had not posted about the incident on its official X account at the time of writing.

For Call of Duty players, talk of bombs and explosions is ordinary match commentary. Search and Destroy, one of the series’ best-known modes, is built entirely around planting or defusing a bomb, and explosives such as C4 and grenades are standard equipment. The mode is a fixture of competitive Call of Duty, and it returns in this year’s Modern Warfare 4, which drew mixed reactions at launch . Out of context, a single excited line from a match can sound alarming to anyone sitting nearby.

title: BIG débarque en RLCS
content:
Le mercato continue de s’agiter sur Rocket League, et cette fois, c’est un nouveau géant de l’esport allemand qui pourrait entrer dans la danse. Selon les informations de Sheep Esports , BIG serait sur le point de recruter Damian « Tox » Schäfer, Matheo « osaft » Hapke et Nico « Nico » Majgren, trois joueurs libres ayant annoncé leur association le 23 octobre dernier. Une arrivée historique pour l’organisation berlinoise, fondée en 2017 et particulièrement connue pour ses équipes sur Counter-Strike et League of Legends. BIG a également connu le succès sur Fortnite, avec notamment un sacre à l’Esports World Cup, et souhaiterait désormais étendre ses activités à Rocket League.

Pour ses premiers pas sur la scène compétitive, BIG miserait sur un mélange d’expérience et de jeunesse. Présent en RLCS depuis 2020, Tox apporterait son vécu au groupe, après avoir notamment terminé deuxième des qualifications européennes de la dernière chance pour les Worlds 2026 avec Volare. À ses côtés, le Danois Nico, âgé de 17 ans, sort d’une saison encourageante chez NOVO Esports, tandis que son homologue allemand osaft, également âgé de 17 ans, s’est illustré sur la scène du 1v1. Demi-finaliste de l’European 1v1 Open en 2026, ce dernier avait notamment remporté le championnat d’Europe FIFAe avec Tox sous les couleurs de l’Allemagne. Le trio serait accompagné de l’entraîneur norvégien Kasper « Kasper » Sjølstad, ancien membre de WYLDE.

Cette nouvelle formation devrait rapidement avoir l’occasion de se mesurer aux meilleures équipes européennes. Le trio figure parmi les candidats les plus sérieux aux qualifications ouvertes du London Club Kick-Off, aux côtés notamment de Geekay Esports et d’Ikkaku, la nouvelle équipe formée par Rezears, yujin et le Français ExoTiiK. Un premier rendez-vous important pour BIG, qui ne fait pas partie des 20 organisations invitées à intégrer le programme de partenariat des RLCS 2027.

L’organisation allemande aurait d’ailleurs dû faire face à une concurrence importante pour s’attacher les services du trio. Toujours selon la même source, l’Eintracht Francfort, également présent sur League of Legends, aurait tenté sa chance, tout comme Five Fears et NOVO Esports. BIG semble finalement avoir pris l’avantage dans ce dossier, même si aucune signature n’a encore été officialisée. Avec un vétéran expérimenté et deux jeunes talents prometteurs, la structure berlinoise pourrait rapidement se faire une place parmi les outsiders de la scène européenne.

title: After Activision apologizes, moves to trim real Itaewon crush footage from Modern Warfare 4, Korea’s game regulator is unimpressed
content:
Activision will remove real footage of the 2022 Itaewon crowd crush from Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 in an update on 12 November. The decision follows protests from the families of the 159 people who died, who condemned the clip’s use in the game’s opening cinematic. The publisher apologised on 30 October, a week after launch, saying it had never meant to evoke or make light of any real tragedy. South Korea’s game regulator has made it clear, however, that taking the clip out will not settle the matter, and it is now looking at how the footage got past the country’s age-rating process.

The clip lasts about three seconds and appears in a montage of news reports about a fictional North Korean invasion of the South, which is how the campaign opens. Players identified it as real broadcast footage of people performing CPR on a victim in Itaewon on 29 October 2022. That night, a Halloween crowd crush in a narrow alley became one of the worst peacetime disasters in South Korea’s recent history. Modern Warfare 4 had launched worldwide on 23 October, only six days before the fourth anniversary, and its Korean War setting had already dragged the game into South Korean politics .

The 10·29 Itaewon Disaster Bereaved Families Association and a coalition of civic groups issued a joint statement on 28 October. They said they could not help but be appalled that scenes of citizens performing CPR had been “used unchanged to create a scene in a game”. They added that many people who helped with the rescue, or simply witnessed the disaster, are still living with trauma, and called the use of the tragedy as entertainment highly inappropriate. The families also pointed to hateful comments online that mocked the disaster by linking the crush to the game’s war setting.

The Korea Game Users Association, which speaks for players rather than the industry, backed the demand on the same day. It said real disaster footage “unrelated to the game’s progression” had revived the families’ pain, and asked Activision to explain why the clip was needed, apologise to those affected and replace it. Activision’s first response, given to Yonhap News Agency, was far more guarded. It said a few real news scenes had been used to convey the game’s fictional story, and that it had no intention of referencing or trivialising the Itaewon disaster. It did not, however, say whether the footage would be removed.

The tone changed completely when Activision spoke again two days later, in a statement sent to Korean media on 30 October. It described Modern Warfare 4 as “a work of fiction created to provide realistic immersion” and apologised to the bereaved families and victims. It also said the footage “will be completely removed” in the 12 November update. Infinity Ward’s Season 1 patch notes , published on 5 November, contain only one line for the campaign, on performance fixes. They make no mention of the cinematic, which leaves next week’s update as the date to watch.

The row has also reached the government, which is where the bigger questions for Activision now sit. Yun Ho-jung, the head of the Ministry of the Interior and Safety , told a press briefing on 29 October that including the footage amounted to “secondary harm” and that “appropriate sanctions should be imposed”. He added that any decision to punish the game or block access to it belonged to the relevant agencies. That phrase carries real weight in South Korea, where the Cabinet passed a revision to the Itaewon special act in February to give legal grounds for punishing the secondary victimisation of those affected by the crush.

title: Modern Warfare 4 Season 1 Weapon Buffs and Nerfs: Every Gun That Changed

title: What are Kill Modes in Modern Warfare 4? Answered
content:
There are dozens of different challenges available to complete in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4. From weapon Mastery Camos to daily challenges to Prestige challenges, there’s always something for you to be working towards in multiplayer and DMZ. However, if you opt to try and go for some of the calling card challenges in Modern Warfare 4, you’ll need to know what Kill Modes are.

You’re required to play “Kill Modes” for a variety of different calling card challenges in MW4, so here’s what they are and how to play them.

Fortunately, there’s a very simple explanation for what Kill Modes are in MW4. Plain and simple, they are game modes where the sole objective is to kill the enemy team. Any game mode with a side objective, such as collecting dog tags in Kill Confirmed, cash in Inflation, or capturing flags in Domination, isn’t considered a Kill Mode since score isn’t determined by kills alone.

As you might expect by now, there aren’t too many confirmed Kill Modes in MW4. However, the two Kill Modes are hugely popular, and they’re Team Deathmatch and Free-For-All . Playing either TDM or FFA in MW4 counts as playing a Kill Mode, so these modes will progress any challenge that requires that specific mode in multiplayer.

We recommend playing Team Deathmatch for most Kill Mode challenges, as you have easier opportunities to kill enemy players and there’s a team around you to help out with scorestreaks. However, if you want the most chances possible to kill enemies, then Free-For-All is the way to go, as no teammate can steal your potential kills.

In any case, you now have a guaranteed way to get kills while playing Kill Modes in Modern Warfare 4. With that out of the way, you can move on to completing other challenges, such as getting Longshot Kills or Point Blank Kills .

title: How to get Point Blank Kills in Modern Warfare 4
content:
There are some weapon camo challenges throughout Call of Duty history that give players the most trouble. In Modern Warfare 4 , several of these camo challenges have returned, including getting Point Blank Kills. These types of kills have long been a thorn in the side of camo grinders, but there are ways to make getting Point Blanks much easier in multiplayer.

Below, we’ll go through how to get Point Blank Kills and the best ways to go about doing so in Modern Warfare 4 multiplayer.

For starters, a Point Blank Kill is earned when you eliminate an enemy that is in extremely close proximity to you. It doesn’t matter when you damage an enemy, but when you see the kill pop up in the killfeed, you need to be within a certain range of the enemy for it to count as a Point Blank.

The exact range for a Point Blank Kill in Modern Warfare 4 is currently unknown, but we do know that it’s much closer than you might expect. In most cases, you need to be within roughly two meters of an enemy when you kill them to earn a Point Blank. This goes for all weapon classes as well, so unlike Longshot Kills , you have to be roughly two meters away even if you’re using something like a light machine gun or sniper rifle.

Now that you understand what a Point Blank Kill is, what’s the most optimal way to go about earning them in multiplayer? Well, it slightly depends on the gun you’re using, as some weapons are naturally stronger at closer ranges.

However, for the most part, you’ll want to use mobility attachments on your loadout so you can get your gun up quicker, which helps out tremendously when killing enemies at close-range. You could also go for an entirely hip-fire build and just shoot from the hip when killing enemies up close. This works best for most weapons, but you can ADS with something like an SMG or assault rifle and have the same results.

title: How to ‘Complete a Loot Radio Tower Side Op’ in Modern Warfare 4 DMZ
content:
When you’re about halfway through the DMZ Orders in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 , you’ll encounter a task to “Complete a Loot Radio Tower Side Op.” While this sounds simple enough, you might quickly realize that there is no “Loot Radio Tower” mission on the map, so where do you go to complete the Side Op?

Fortunately, we managed to complete this specific Side Op in MW4 DMZ , and we’ll explain exactly how to finish this DMZ Order.

With previous DMZ Orders, all you’ve had to do for missions like this one is look on the map and find a green icon labeled with the mission you’re trying to complete. However, there is no Loot Radio Tower mission labeled on any icon on the map, no matter how hard you look.

Instead, you need to head to one single spot on the map to complete this particular Side Op. Specifically, you need to go to “C6” quadrant in Hajin, which is located north of Deadtown . Here, just east of a Fire Station, you’ll see a blue radio tower that has red smoke coming off the top of it. If you don’t see red smoke, then another player has beaten you to this Side Op, so you’ll have to enter a new match to attempt it again.

When you spot the smoking radio tower, the “Loot Radio Tower” icon will appear on your map, giving you the go-ahead to complete the mission. To start, you need to climb the radio tower, which requires much more parkour than you’re used to in DMZ. You have to jump to poles, climb up ladders, and carefully make your way up the tower until you reach the top.

Once you reach the top, all you have to do is interact with the crate at the top of the tower, and it will complete the Loot Radio Tower Side Op in DMZ. You can loot the crate, which sometimes has decent loot, and after that, the DMZ Order task will be complete, and you can move on to the next one in MW4.

This guide explains how to get the Fortnite Pirate Shop Token, how to activate it, and what it includes. It also covers the main restrictions.

The Fortnite Pirate Shop Token is an extremely rare reward in the Fortnite Treasure Hunters mini season. The mini season launched on November 1, 2026, with update v43.00. It bridges Chapter 7 Season 4 and Chapter 8.

Each token gives two uses. One works in 2026 and the other in 2027. Each use lasts 14 days from the moment a player activates it, which adds up to 28 days of free Item Shop claims.

During an active period, players can claim items sold for V-Bucks in the Item Shop at no cost. Depending on what appears in the shop, the claimed cosmetics could be worth thousands of dollars. Epic Games has not revealed the odds of finding the token.

Players can get the token by opening Chests in Battle Royale during Treasure Hunters. A Chest can trigger a free reward for the squad. Most rewards are Gizmos. Cosmetics and Pirate Shop access are also possible, but the chance is very slim.

title: Vico Opens Up About Mental Health Struggles After Career-Best Fortnite Year
content:
BIG’s Taylor-Petrik “vic0” Gatschelhofer, known to most fans as Vico, has opened up about years of mental health struggles, five weeks after finishing third at the FNCS Global Championship and stepping away from competitive Fortnite. In posts on X on Sunday, he said he attempted to take his own life shortly before Globals, and that he no longer has contact with his family.

Vico’s 2026 run with Malibuca is why BIG called them “the best duo of all time” after Globals. They won the FNCS Major 1 Summit in Düsseldorf , then took the inaugural Fortnite Reload Elite Series at the Esports World Cup 2026.

Globals, at the Lotto Arena in Antwerp from 24 to 27 September, nearly made it three. The BIG pair led by 32 points going into the final game and finished third , four points behind champions SwizzY and Pixie, for $160,000 from the $2,000,000 prize pool. Our Globals grand finals report covers how that last game unfolded.

BIG’s chief gaming officer, Roman Reinhardt, summed up the result at the time: “Third place at Fortnite Globals. So close, but that’s part of it and it stings. Not everyone can say they were one kill away from the Globals win.” He added a line aimed at his players: “We believe in you 100%.” The club’s own post on X put it more simply: “No third trophy but still a great result.”

In October, BIG announced that Vico was one of ten finalists for Esports PC Player of the Year at the Esports Awards 2026, with the winners due to be revealed in Miami on 17 November. “Vico has had an incredible year, and his journey is truly special,” Reinhardt said then. Vico called the nomination “a huge honour”.

The first sign that something was wrong came on the final day of Globals. Vico said he had almost not attended the event, a comment picked up and shared by community accounts within hours. That evening he announced a break on X : “will be taking a break from competetive fortnite for a while. dealing with a lot of private stuff outside my competetive carreer and want to focus on that first and figure my life out. Will be back next year.”

title: RLCS : Vitality frappe fort avec nass, Oski et diaz (off.)

Ce mercredi soir, Gentle Mates a officialisé le recrutement d’Alexis « zen » Bernier, Axel « Vatira » Touret et Tristan « Atow » Soyez, donnant naissance à une véritable super-équipe francophone. Un trio dont l’association faisait rêver une partie de la communauté depuis plusieurs mois, mais dont la concrétisation était loin d’être acquise. Gentle Mates a dû livrer une bataille particulièrement intense face à la Karmine Corp et Vitality, également déterminées à attirer ces trois stars. Les négociations auraient été marquées par une importante surenchère et plusieurs tensions en coulisses, avant que le club fondé par Squeezie, Brawks et Gotaga ne parvienne à convaincre les joueurs.

Ce transfert marque également la fin de deux aventures emblématiques du Rocket League français. Arrivé chez Vitality en 2023, zen avait immédiatement bouleversé la hiérarchie mondiale, remportant les Championnats du monde dès sa première saison professionnelle. De son côté, Vatira quitte la Karmine Corp après quatre années durant lesquelles il est devenu le véritable visage de la section Rocket League, avec notamment trois Majors remportés. Atow, son coéquipier depuis 2024, apporte lui aussi une immense expérience du très haut niveau, après avoir notamment remporté l’Esports World Cup 2025 sous les couleurs de la KC.

Sur le papier, Gentle Mates possède désormais l’un des effectifs les plus impressionnants de l’histoire de Rocket League. Les trois joueurs, déjà habitués à évoluer ensemble ou à se retrouver sur les plus grandes scènes internationales, devront toutefois transformer cette accumulation de talents en résultats. Car les attentes seront immenses autour d’une formation qui ne pourra raisonnablement viser autre chose que les plus grands trophées.

La concurrence s’annonce d’ailleurs particulièrement relevée en France. Dans la foulée de ces départs, la Karmine Corp a officialisé son nouveau projet autour de M0nkey M00n, bibbaba et reyyn, avec Extra toujours aux commandes. Vitality, de son côté, restera également engagée sur le circuit RLCS malgré le départ de sa star. Trois structures françaises, des effectifs profondément remaniés et une rivalité qui promet de faire des étincelles : la prochaine saison, dont le coup d’envoi est prévu à la mi-novembre, s’annonce déjà passionnante.

title: RLCS : AcroniK prend sa retraite à seulement 21 ans

Une page se tourne sur la scène européenne de Rocket League. Bruno Alexandre « AcroniK » dos Santos Lopes a officialisé sa retraite sportive à seulement 21 ans, dans un court message publié sur les réseaux sociaux. « Je sais que ce ne sont pas les meilleurs mots pour annoncer une retraite, mais honnêtement, je n’ai pas envie d’écrire un long texte pour dire que j’arrête. Merci à tous. On se retrouve pour le prochain chapitre ! » , a confié le Portugais, sans donner davantage de détails sur ses futurs projets.

C’est surtout sous les couleurs de Team Liquid qu’AcroniK s’est fait un nom, en accompagnant l’éclosion de deux jeunes prodiges : Tristan « Atow » Soyez et Oskar « Oski » Gozdowski. Recrutés en février 2022 alors qu’ils n’avaient que 14 ans, les deux joueurs ont rapidement formé avec lui l’un des trios les plus redoutables d’Europe. Ensemble, ils ont remporté deux tournois régionaux, participé à cinq LAN internationales et atteint le dernier carré des Worlds 2023. Une aventure qui reste aujourd’hui le sommet de la carrière du Portugais, considéré comme le joueur le plus accompli de son pays sur Rocket League.

Après la séparation du trio en 2023, AcroniK n’a jamais vraiment retrouvé les mêmes résultats. Il s’est néanmoins illustré chez Luna Galaxy, avec notamment une deuxième place lors d’un tournoi régional des RLCS 2024, après une courte défaite face à BDS (3-4). Plus récemment, il avait rejoint NOVO Esports pour la saison 2026, disputant plusieurs tournois régionaux avant de représenter le Portugal aux championnats continentaux FIFAe, où sa sélection a atteint le top 8.

AcroniK quitte ainsi la scène professionnelle après sept années de compétition et six LAN des RLCS disputées au total. Il rejoint une liste de joueurs ayant récemment annoncé leur retraite, parmi lesquels ApparentlyJack, Comm, Stake et LuiisP. Si son palmarès ne reflète pas forcément toute son influence, le Portugais laisse derrière lui un héritage important, notamment pour son rôle dans l’éclosion d’Atow et Oski, aujourd’hui encore présents au plus haut niveau.

title: RLCS : Extra reste fidèle à la Karmine Corp, le retour d’un duo légendaire

Un choix important pour l’organisation française, contrainte de revoir entièrement ses plans après les départs attendus d’Atow et Vatira vers Gentle Mates. Extra avait lui-même discuté avec cette dernière structure pour suivre ses anciens joueurs, avant de finalement privilégier la continuité avec la KC.

Arrivé à la Karmine Corp après avoir pris sa retraite de joueur en 2025, le Français de 24 ans sort d’une première saison réussie sur le banc. Mais son maintien prend une dimension particulière avec l’arrivée attendue d’Evan « M0nkey M00n » Rogez, son ancien coéquipier chez Team BDS. Ensemble, les deux Français avaient remporté les Worlds RLCS 2021-2022, avant de marquer durablement l’histoire de la scène compétitive. Ils pourraient désormais se retrouver dans une configuration inédite, avec Extra dans le rôle d’entraîneur et M0nkey M00n comme leader sur le terrain.

Après avoir envisagé un retrait de Rocket League durant l’intersaison, la Karmine Corp aurait finalement choisi de miser sur un mélange d’expérience et de jeunesse. M0nkey M00n devrait être accompagné d’Attila « bibbaba » Eötvös et de reyyn, deux joueurs de seulement 16 ans, encore peu expérimentés au plus haut niveau. Un pari ambitieux, mais qui permettrait aux deux espoirs d’évoluer aux côtés d’un double champion du monde, sous les ordres d’un entraîneur qui connaît parfaitement son jeu.

Cette nouvelle équipe aurait pour mission de tourner la page d’un effectif historique, également marqué par le départ attendu de juicy vers Geekay Esports. La KC devrait faire ses premiers pas avec ce trio lors du RLCS Kick-Off de Londres en décembre, une compétition à laquelle elle est invitée en tant qu’organisation partenaire. Après une intersaison mouvementée, le club français semble donc avoir trouvé les bases de son nouveau projet, avec des ambitions à reconstruire autour du duo Extra – M0nkey M00n.

title: Razer controllers will power Rocket League student finals at FUSE Esports Festival
content:
Student finalists in the State and National Rocket League Finals will play on high-end Razer controllers used by professional players this November, after the hardware brand became the Official Controller Partner of Australian school esports operator The FUSE Cup. The Rocket League decider is the capstone of a school year of qualifiers.

The FUSE Cup's Chief Operating Officer, Daniel Aivaliotis-Martinez, shared the news in an announcement post on LinkedIn , which he used to speak about creating meaningful experiences for young people before thanking the Razer team for their support and belief in what the FUSE Cup is building. Razer gear, which is used by esports pros around the world, as well as actual world champions, will now be in the hands of every finalist competing for the national title.

The controllers themselves come with 2.4GHz wireless technology that prevents lag, toggleable physical triggers and back paddles.

The partnership has two parts: finalists get Razer controllers for the State and National Rocket League Finals, which means players won’t have to bring their own pads to the biggest series of their school careers.

Secondly, Razer is sponsoring the Student Leadership Award, a new category at the FUSE Australian School Esports Awards. It's aimed at pupils who make a positive contribution to their community and show leadership inside their school's esports program. It means the brand is also putting itself on a prize that has nothing to do with winning matches.

The FUSE Esports Festival sees itself as Australia's largest in-person school esports festival. It’s backed by the City of Gold Coast council, and it takes place at Southern Cross University.

title: La Coupe de France Slash est de retour sur Rocket League
content:
La Coupe de France Slash de Rocket League s’apprête à faire son grand retour pour une deuxième édition. Après avoir attiré 1,8 million de vues en direct cumulées en 2025, l’événement renouvelle son partenariat avec France Télévisions et sa plateforme Slash. L’an dernier, Gentle Mates avait remporté le trophée face à la Karmine Corp lors de la finale organisée à la Paris Games Week. Cette fois, la compétition se déroulera entièrement en ligne et permettra aux nouvelles compositions de se mesurer avant la reprise du circuit professionnel.

Le tournoi se tiendra du 28 octobre au 12 novembre, avec une diffusion exclusive des phases de poule du 2 au 11 novembre, avant les demi-finales et la grande finale programmées le 12 novembre. L’ensemble des rencontres sera accessible gratuitement sur les chaînes Twitch et YouTube de Slash, ainsi que sur ses comptes X et TikTok. Les commentaires seront assurés par RocketBaguette, collectif incontournable de la scène francophone Rocket League.

Avec cette deuxième édition, France Télévisions confirme sa volonté de renforcer la visibilité de l’esport auprès du grand public. La Coupe de France Slash constituera également un premier rendez-vous intéressant pour observer les nouveaux effectifs de la scène française, dans un mercato particulièrement mouvementé à l’approche des RLCS 2027.

title: RLCS : ExoTiiK va rebondir avec yujin et Rezears
content:
Le mercato Rocket League continue de s’agiter en Europe. Brice « ExoTiiK » Bigeard a officialisé ce vendredi la création d’une nouvelle équipe avec Liam « yujin » Daillac et David « Rezears » Wünsch. Les trois joueurs, actuellement libres de tout contrat, disputeront les qualifications ouvertes du RLCS Kick-Off Open avec l’ambition de décrocher l’unique place disponible pour le London Kick-Off Weekend. Le Français Thomas « Ekon » Chenel, ancien sélectionneur de l’équipe de France lors des FIFAe Continental Championships, accompagnera le trio en tant qu’entraîneur. Dans son annonce, ExoTiiK a également précisé que l’effectif était toujours à la recherche d’une organisation pour la saison prochaine.

Ce nouveau projet marque un rebond rapide pour ExoTiiK, dont le départ de Vitality a été officialisé le 20 octobre. Après deux saisons chez les Abeilles, le champion du monde 2024 avait notamment atteint la finale du Major de Boston aux côtés de zen et stizzy, avant de participer aux Worlds 2026. Son départ intervient alors que Vitality prépare une reconstruction autour de nass, Oski et diaz, un trio qui aurait déjà trouvé un accord verbal avec l’organisation française.

Ses deux nouveaux coéquipiers ont également des raisons de vouloir se relancer. Âgé de 18 ans, yujin avait été envisagé par la Karmine Corp durant ce mercato, avant que le club ne privilégie finalement bibbaba pour accompagner M0nkey M00n et reyyn. De son côté, Rezears a multiplié les expériences au sein d’équipes sans structure en 2026, sans parvenir à se qualifier pour un événement international. L’Allemand était néanmoins passé tout près des championnats du monde, terminant dans le top 4 des qualifications de la dernière chance en Europe.

Avec l’expérience internationale d’ExoTiiK et le potentiel de ses deux partenaires, ce nouvel effectif s’annonce comme l’un des principaux prétendants à la qualification pour Londres. Reste à savoir si ses performances permettront également de convaincre une organisation de soutenir le projet pour les RLCS 2027.

title: RLCS : Vitality confirme le départ de zen
content:
C’est la fin d’une aventure qui aura marqué l’esport français. Team Vitality a officialisé ce vendredi le départ d’Alexis « zen » Bernier, recruté en février 2022 alors qu’il n’avait que 15 ans. Dans un message publié sur ses réseaux sociaux, l’organisation a rendu hommage à son joueur emblématique : « L’enfant prodige s’envole vers de nouveaux horizons… Aucun mot n’est assez fort pour saluer la légende que tu as écrite chez Vitality. » Arrivé sur la scène RLCS en 2023, zen avait immédiatement bouleversé la hiérarchie mondiale, enchaînant cinq titres consécutifs avec Alpha54 et Radosin, jusqu’au sacre historique lors des championnats du monde 2023. Un début de carrière exceptionnel qui l’a rapidement installé parmi les meilleurs joueurs de la planète.

Si sa prochaine destination n’a pas encore été officialisée, zen devrait rejoindre Gentle Mates pour les RLCS 2027. Le Français formerait un trio particulièrement attendu avec Atow et Vatira, eux aussi sur le départ de la Karmine Corp. Les trois joueurs auraient étudié les propositions des principales structures françaises avant de privilégier le projet des Mates, qui doivent encore finaliser les accords nécessaires à leur recrutement. Déjà sacré champion du monde en 2v2 avec Atow cette année, zen avait affiché sa volonté de poursuivre l’aventure aux côtés du Belge.

Son départ oblige désormais Vitality à reconstruire entièrement son effectif Rocket League. L’organisation aurait déjà trouvé un accord verbal avec nass, Oski et diaz pour la saison prochaine. De son côté, zen quitte les Abeilles avec un palmarès impressionnant, comprenant un titre mondial, six victoires en régionale européenne et douze participations à des événements internationaux des RLCS. À seulement 19 ans, il s’apprête à ouvrir un nouveau chapitre de sa carrière, après avoir écrit l’une des plus belles pages de l’histoire de Vitality.

title: RLCS : FaZe Clan prépare son grand retour avec un trio brésilien
content:
C’est un nom historique de l’esport qui s’apprête à retrouver Rocket League. Selon les informations de Sheep Esports , FaZe Clan aurait trouvé un accord verbal avec Gabriel « Lostt » Buzon, Bernardo « Bemmz » Marta et Cauã « crn » Cerione pour former son nouvel effectif. La structure américaine, invitée à rejoindre le programme de partenariat du RLCS Club Championship, aurait donc choisi de s’implanter en Amérique du Sud. Lostt, qui évoluait depuis plus de trois ans chez FURIA, serait la tête d’affiche de ce projet. Il retrouverait Bemmz, son ancien coéquipier chez The Club lors de la saison 2022-2023, ainsi que l’entraîneur Nicolas « Michi » Michikoviski, également passé par cette formation. De son côté, crn arrive après une saison disputée sous les couleurs de BS+COMPETITION.

Présent sur Rocket League entre 2021 et 2023, FaZe Clan avait marqué la scène nord-américaine avec une équipe emmenée par Firstkiller. L’organisation avait notamment participé à sept événements internationaux des RLCS et deux championnats du monde, atteignant la finale du Winter Major 2023. Elle avait finalement quitté la discipline après le Gamers8 2023, dans un contexte de restructuration. Désormais séparée de FaZe Media, la branche esport du groupe, détenue par GameSquare et dirigée par Kaysan, entend relancer son aventure sur le jeu d’Epic Games.

Avant de se tourner vers ce trio brésilien, FaZe avait exploré plusieurs pistes, notamment celle menant à diaz, finalement attendu chez Team Vitality, ainsi qu’au duo Motta-DRUFINHO, qui devrait rejoindre M80 avec Joreuz. L’organisation aurait finalement privilégié Lostt, Bemmz et crn, trois joueurs expérimentés sur la scène sud-américaine. Si leur recrutement se confirme, ils devraient faire leurs débuts sous leurs nouvelles couleurs lors du London Kick-Off Weekend en décembre, avant de participer aux RLCS 2027. Un retour qui s’inscrit dans une vague d’arrivées et de retours d’organisations majeures sur Rocket League, aux côtés notamment de Team Heretics, AG.AL et Wolves Esports.

title: RLCS : la Karmine Corp va reconstruire autour de M0nkey M00n
content:
C’est un tournant majeur qui se prépare chez Karmine Corp. Selon les informations de Sheep Esports , Evan « M0nkey M00n » Rogez devrait rejoindre le club de Kameto pour la saison 2027 des RLCS, aux côtés du Hongrois Attila « bibbaba » Eötvös et du jeune Français reyyn. Un projet mêlant expérience et jeunesse, alors que la structure doit reconstruire intégralement son effectif après les départs attendus d’Atow et Vatira vers Gentle Mates, ainsi que celui de juicy vers Geekay Esports. Plusieurs autres pistes avaient été étudiées, notamment prozy, finalement attendu chez Ninjas in Pyjamas, et l’ancien joueur de Gentle Mates yujin.

Double champion du monde et finaliste du Major de Paris avec Twisted Minds, M0nkey M00n devrait ainsi retrouver l’Europe après une saison passée dans la région MENA. Le Français de 23 ans, longtemps adversaire de la Karmine Corp sous les couleurs de BDS et Vitality, apporterait son expérience à deux joueurs encore peu habitués au plus haut niveau. Bibbaba s’est notamment illustré en atteignant le top 6 des qualifications européennes de la dernière chance pour les Worlds 2026, tandis que reyyn, spécialiste du 1v1, n’a encore jamais disputé de compétition RLCS.

Ce recrutement marquerait également un changement de stratégie important pour la Karmine Corp, qui avait sérieusement envisagé de se retirer de Rocket League après avoir perdu la bataille pour conserver Atow et Vatira. Kameto avait alors évoqué deux possibilités : recruter des joueurs confirmés encore disponibles ou repartir avec de très jeunes talents. Avec M0nkey M00n, bibbaba et reyyn, le club semble finalement avoir choisi de combiner les deux approches. Un pari ambitieux pour une équipe qui devra désormais se reconstruire autour d’une légende de la scène française et de deux espoirs prometteurs.

title: AG.AL a trouvé son trio pour les RLCS 2027
content:
Après avoir été invitée à rejoindre le programme de partenariat des RLCS 2027, AG.AL aurait verrouillé son premier roster sur Rocket League. Selon les informations de Sheep Esports , la structure chinoise est sur le point de signer Joseph « Joyo » Young, Archie « Archie » Pickthall et Ole « oaly. » Doorn, avec Dylan « eekso » Pickering au poste d’entraîneur. Une réunion particulièrement intéressante puisque les quatre hommes avaient déjà travaillé ensemble chez Geekay Esports en 2025, terminant dans le top 4 des Championnats du monde. AG.AL avait initialement tenté de se positionner sur le trio français Atow, Vatira et zen, désormais proche de Gentle Mates, avant de se tourner vers d’autres pistes.

Archie devrait donc quitter Gentle Mates après une saison marquée par la victoire au Major de Boston 2026, tandis qu’Oaly est libre depuis son départ de Ninjas in Pyjamas en septembre. De son côté, Joyo sort d’une année plus compliquée avec Geekay Esports, durant laquelle il n’a pas réussi à se qualifier pour les Worlds, une première depuis ses débuts sur le circuit RLCS. Les trois joueurs espèrent désormais retrouver leur complémentarité et reproduire les performances réalisées ensemble en 2025.

Pour AG.AL, cette arrivée sur Rocket League s’inscrit dans une stratégie de développement ambitieuse. L’organisation chinoise, récemment récompensée lors de l’Esports World Cup Club Championship, dispose de moyens importants pour renforcer sa présence sur plusieurs disciplines. Avec un trio expérimenté et un entraîneur qui connaît déjà parfaitement ses joueurs, elle pourrait rapidement s’imposer comme une prétendante sérieuse sur la scène européenne. Sa nouvelle équipe devrait faire ses débuts lors du Club Kick-off à Londres.

title: RLCS : NIP mise sur un prodige de 15 ans pour compléter son roster
content:

Il avait notamment atteint le dernier carré des qualifications européennes de la dernière chance pour les Worlds 2026 aux côtés de cocoo et Shark, avant de s’incliner face aux futurs vainqueurs, Mate y Tapa. Plus récemment, il a également remporté la Bubble World Cup avec la Suisse, en battant la France en finale.

Le recrutement de prozy permettrait à Ninjas in Pyjamas de finaliser son équipe pour 2027, après le départ de Joreuz vers M80 en Amérique du Nord. L’organisation suédoise devrait ainsi reconstruire son effectif autour de crr, déjà présent la saison dernière, et de stizzy, qui quitte Team Vitality après une année marquée notamment par une deuxième place au Major de Boston. Le duo espagnol apporterait son expérience du plus haut niveau pour accompagner l’un des jeunes talents les plus prometteurs de la scène européenne.

Avec deux joueurs expérimentés et un prodige de 15 ans, la structure espère franchir un cap sur la scène internationale.

title: RLCS : Vitality officialise le départ d’ExoTiiK
content:
Le grand ménage se poursuit chez Team Vitality. Après deux saisons sous les couleurs des Abeilles, Brice « ExoTiiK » Bigeard quitte officiellement l’organisation, comme annoncé ce mardi sur les réseaux sociaux. Arrivé en octobre 2024 après son sacre mondial avec Team BDS, où il avait également été élu MVP des Worlds, le Français de 23 ans aura participé à sept événements internationaux des RLCS avec Vitality. Une aventure marquée par plusieurs belles performances, notamment une finale au Major de Boston et des places dans le dernier carré à Raleigh et Paris. Mais les résultats aux championnats du monde n’ont pas été à la hauteur des ambitions, avec deux éliminations consécutives entre la 9e et la 12e place en 2025 et 2026.

Ce départ s’inscrit dans une reconstruction complète de l’effectif Rocket League de Vitality. Selon les informations de Sheep Esports , l’organisation aurait déjà trouvé des accords verbaux avec nass, Oski et diaz pour former son nouveau trio. De son côté, zen se rapproche de Gentle Mates, où il pourrait rejoindre Atow et Vatira, tandis que stizzy devrait poursuivre sa carrière chez Ninjas in Pyjamas. Pour la première fois depuis son arrivée sur Rocket League, Vitality pourrait donc aligner une équipe sans aucun joueur français.

Seul rescapé attendu de l’effectif précédent, le coach belge Eversax devrait conserver son poste pour accompagner ce nouveau projet. Quant à ExoTiiK, il se retrouve désormais libre d’explorer ses options sur le marché des transferts, alors que plusieurs organisations engagées dans le prochain RLCS Club Championship n’ont pas encore finalisé leur composition. À 23 ans, l’ancien champion du monde dispose encore d’un solide palmarès pour séduire une nouvelle équipe.

title: RLCS : Eversax reste chez Vitality
content:
Un temps annoncé sur le marché après l’expiration de son contrat, Benjamin « Eversax » Wagner devrait finalement rester chez Team Vitality pour la saison 2027. Selon les informations de Sheep Esports , l’entraîneur belge aurait trouvé un accord verbal avec l’organisation française pour poursuivre sa mission à la tête de l’équipe. Arrivé en octobre 2025 aux côtés de stizzy, il serait ainsi le seul membre de l’effectif 2026 à conserver sa place. Vitality aurait en effet déjà trouvé des accords avec nass, Oski et diaz, trois joueurs appelés à former son nouveau trio après les départs attendus de zen, stizzy et ExoTiiK.

Ce renouvellement marque un tournant majeur pour la structure française. Après plusieurs saisons passées sous les couleurs des Abeilles, zen se rapproche de Gentle Mates, où il pourrait retrouver Atow et Vatira pour former une véritable équipe de stars. Stizzy devrait quant à lui rejoindre Ninjas in Pyjamas aux côtés de crr, tandis qu’ExoTiiK devrait également céder sa place. Pour la première fois depuis son arrivée sur Rocket League, Vitality pourrait donc évoluer sans aucun joueur français, Eversax restant le seul représentant francophone de l’effectif.

Ancien entraîneur de la Karmine Corp et de Gentle Mates, Eversax possède une solide expérience du plus haut niveau, avec notamment un sacre au Major de Copenhague en 2024. Lors des RLCS 2026, il avait accompagné Vitality jusqu’à la deuxième place du Major de Boston et dans le dernier carré à Paris, avant une élimination décevante entre la 9e et la 12e place aux Worlds. Avec un trio entièrement renouvelé, le technicien belge aura désormais la lourde tâche de lancer un nouveau cycle et de ramener les Abeilles au sommet de Rocket League.
